# I. Data importation & Exploration

```{r}
library(pacman)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(skimr)
library(VIM)
library(summarytools)
library(corrplot)
library(janitor)
library(purrr)


setwd("C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy")
# Load the data - using semicolon as separator based on the CSV structure
data <- read.csv("BD_rdt.csv", sep = ";", dec = ",", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Display basic information about the dataset
cat("Dataset dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Number of columns:", ncol(data), "\n")

# Display column names
cat("\nColumn names:\n")
print(colnames(data))



```

## I.1. Basic dataset information

```{r}
# Basic dataset information
cat("1. BASIC DATASET INFORMATION\n")
cat("===========================\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(data), "rows x", ncol(data), "columns\n")
cat("Column names:\n")
print(names(data))
cat("\n")

# Data types overview
cat("2. DATA TYPES OVERVIEW\n")
cat("======================\n")
print(glimpse(data))
cat("\n")

# Campaign Analysis
cat("3. CAMPAIGN ANALYSIS\n")
cat("====================\n")
campaign_summary <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise(
    n_observations = n(),
    n_parcelles = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    n_blocks = n_distinct(Bloc),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Camp)

print("Observations per Campaign:")
print(campaign_summary)

cat("\nCampaign period coverage:")
cat("From", min(data$Camp, na.rm = TRUE), "to", max(data$Camp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Total campaigns:", n_distinct(data$Camp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n\n")

# Block and Parcelle Analysis
cat("4. BLOCK AND PARCELLE STRUCTURE ANALYSIS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Parcelles per block
parcelle_per_block <- data %>%
  group_by(Bloc) %>%
  summarise(
    n_parcelles = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    campaigns = paste(sort(unique(Camp)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_parcelles))

print("Parcelles per Block:")
print(parcelle_per_block)

# Block consistency across campaigns
block_campaign <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise(
    blocks = list(sort(unique(Bloc))),
    n_blocks = n_distinct(Bloc),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

print("\nBlocks per Campaign:")
print(block_campaign %>% select(-blocks))

# Check if blocks are consistent across years
all_blocks <- unique(unlist(block_campaign$blocks))
cat("\nTotal unique blocks across all campaigns:", length(all_blocks), "\n")
print("Unique blocks:")
print(all_blocks)

# Parcelle naming pattern analysis
cat("\n5. PARCELLE NAMING PATTERN ANALYSIS\n")
cat("===================================\n")
parcelle_pattern <- data %>%
  mutate(
    parcelle_prefix = str_extract(Parcelle, "^[^0-9]+"),
    parcelle_number = str_extract(Parcelle, "[0-9]+")
  ) %>%
  group_by(parcelle_prefix) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    unique_parcelles = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

print("Parcelle naming patterns:")
print(parcelle_pattern)

# Evolution of parcelles over time
parcelle_evolution <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise(
    parcelles = list(sort(unique(Parcelle))),
    n_parcelles = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Camp)

print("\nParcelle count evolution over campaigns:")
print(parcelle_evolution %>% select(-parcelles))
```

## I.2. Block and parcel change detection analysis

```{r}
# BLOCK AND PARCEL CHANGE DETECTION ANALYSIS
# ==========================================

cat("6. ADVANCED CHANGE DETECTION ANALYSIS\n")
cat("=====================================\n")

# Create comprehensive change tracking datasets
change_data <- data %>%
  select(Camp, Bloc, Parcelle) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(Camp, Bloc, Parcelle)

# 1. Block-level change analysis
block_changes <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise(
    blocks_present = list(sort(unique(Bloc))),
    n_blocks = n_distinct(Bloc),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Camp) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate changes from previous campaign
    blocks_added = map2(blocks_present, lag(blocks_present, 1), 
                       ~setdiff(.x, .y %||% character(0))),
    blocks_removed = map2(lag(blocks_present, 1), blocks_present,
                         ~setdiff(.x %||% character(0), .y)),
    blocks_continued = map2(blocks_present, lag(blocks_present, 1),
                           ~intersect(.x, .y %||% character(0))),
    n_added = map_int(blocks_added, length),
    n_removed = map_int(blocks_removed, length),
    n_continued = map_int(blocks_continued, length)
  )

# 2. Parcel-level change analysis
parcel_changes <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise(
    parcels_present = list(sort(unique(Parcelle))),
    n_parcels = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Camp) %>%
  mutate(
    parcels_added = map2(parcels_present, lag(parcels_present, 1),
                        ~setdiff(.x, .y %||% character(0))),
    parcels_removed = map2(lag(parcels_present, 1), parcels_present,
                          ~setdiff(.x %||% character(0), .y)),
    parcels_continued = map2(parcels_present, lag(parcels_present, 1),
                            ~intersect(.x, .y %||% character(0))),
    n_added = map_int(parcels_added, length),
    n_removed = map_int(parcels_removed, length),
    n_continued = map_int(parcels_continued, length)
  )

# 3. Block-parcel structure changes
block_parcel_structure <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp, Bloc) %>%
  summarise(
    n_parcels = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    parcels = list(sort(unique(Parcelle))),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Camp, Bloc)

# Calculate structural changes within blocks
block_structure_changes <- block_parcel_structure %>%
  group_by(Bloc) %>%
  arrange(Camp) %>%
  mutate(
    prev_n_parcels = lag(n_parcels),
    parcel_change = n_parcels - (prev_n_parcels %||% n_parcels),
    prev_parcels = lag(parcels),
    parcels_added_in_block = map2(parcels, prev_parcels,
                                 ~setdiff(.x, .y %||% character(0))),
    parcels_removed_in_block = map2(prev_parcels, parcels,
                                   ~setdiff(.x %||% character(0), .y)),
    n_added_in_block = map_int(parcels_added_in_block, length),
    n_removed_in_block = map_int(parcels_removed_in_block, length)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# VISUALIZATION 1: Block Evolution Over Time
plot_block_evolution <- block_changes %>%
  select(Camp, n_blocks, n_added, n_removed, n_continued) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(n_added, n_removed, n_continued),
               names_to = "change_type", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(
    change_type = factor(change_type, 
                        levels = c("n_continued", "n_added", "n_removed"),
                        labels = c("Continued", "Added", "Removed")),
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = count, fill = change_type)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.8, position = "stack") +
  geom_line(data = block_changes %>% 
              mutate(Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))),
            aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = n_blocks), 
            color = "black", size = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = block_changes %>% 
               mutate(Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))),
             aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = n_blocks),
             color = "black", size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Continued" = "#2E8B57", "Added" = "#4682B4", "Removed" = "#CD853F")) +
  labs(
    title = "A. Block Evolution Across Campaigns",
    subtitle = "Stacked areas show block changes, black line shows total blocks",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Number of Blocks",
    fill = "Block Status"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# VISUALIZATION 2: Parcel Evolution Over Time
plot_parcel_evolution <- parcel_changes %>%
  select(Camp, n_parcels, n_added, n_removed, n_continued) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(n_added, n_removed, n_continued),
               names_to = "change_type", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(
    change_type = factor(change_type,
                        levels = c("n_continued", "n_added", "n_removed"),
                        labels = c("Continued", "Added", "Removed")),
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = count, fill = change_type)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.8, position = "stack") +
  geom_line(data = parcel_changes %>%
              mutate(Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))),
            aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = n_parcels),
            color = "black", size = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = parcel_changes %>%
               mutate(Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))),
             aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = n_parcels),
             color = "black", size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Continued" = "#2E8B57", "Added" = "#4682B4", "Removed" = "#CD853F")) +
  labs(
    title = "B. Parcel Evolution Across Campaigns", 
    subtitle = "Stacked areas show parcel changes, black line shows total parcels",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Number of Parcels",
    fill = "Parcel Status"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# VISUALIZATION 3: Heatmap of Block-Parcel Structure
block_parcel_heatmap <- block_parcel_structure %>%
  mutate(Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Campaign_Year), y = reorder(Bloc, n_parcels), fill = n_parcels)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_parcels), color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", name = "Parcels\nper Block") +
  labs(
    title = "C. Block-Parcel Structure Heatmap",
    subtitle = "Number of parcels per block across campaigns",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Block ID"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

# VISUALIZATION 4: Change Magnitude Analysis
change_magnitude <- block_structure_changes %>%
  filter(!is.na(parcel_change)) %>%
  mutate(
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2))),
    change_direction = case_when(
      parcel_change > 0 ~ "Increase",
      parcel_change < 0 ~ "Decrease", 
      TRUE ~ "No Change"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Campaign_Year), y = Bloc, fill = parcel_change)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(parcel_change != 0, 
                              paste0(ifelse(parcel_change > 0, "+", ""), parcel_change), 
                              "")), 
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#CD853F", mid = "white", high = "#4682B4",
                       name = "Parcel\nChange") +
  labs(
    title = "D. Parcel Changes Within Blocks",
    subtitle = "Change in number of parcels per block between campaigns",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Block ID"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

# Combine all plots
combined_change_plots <- (plot_block_evolution | plot_parcel_evolution) / 
                        (block_parcel_heatmap | change_magnitude) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Comprehensive Block and Parcel Change Detection Analysis",
    subtitle = paste("Tracking structural changes across", 
                    length(unique(data$Camp)), "campaigns"),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray60")
    )
  )

# Display the plot
print(combined_change_plots)

# CREATE DETAILED CSV OUTPUTS
# ===========================

# 1. Campaign-by-campaign summary CSV
campaign_summary_detailed <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise(
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp[1], 1, 2))),
    n_observations = n(),
    n_blocks = n_distinct(Bloc),
    n_parcels = n_distinct(Parcelle),
    blocks_list = paste(sort(unique(Bloc)), collapse = "; "),
    parcels_list = paste(sort(unique(Parcelle)), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    block_changes %>% 
      select(Camp, n_added, n_removed, n_continued) %>%
      rename(blocks_added = n_added, blocks_removed = n_removed, blocks_continued = n_continued),
    by = "Camp"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    parcel_changes %>%
      select(Camp, n_added, n_removed, n_continued) %>%
      rename(parcels_added = n_added, parcels_removed = n_removed, parcels_continued = n_continued),
    by = "Camp"
  )

# 2. Detailed change tracking CSV
detailed_changes <- tibble()
for(i in 2:nrow(block_changes)) {
  current_camp <- block_changes$Camp[i]
  prev_camp <- block_changes$Camp[i-1]
  
  # Block changes
  blocks_added <- unlist(block_changes$blocks_added[i])
  blocks_removed <- unlist(block_changes$blocks_removed[i])
  
  # Parcel changes  
  parcels_added <- unlist(parcel_changes$parcels_added[i])
  parcels_removed <- unlist(parcel_changes$parcels_removed[i])
  
  # Create change records
  if(length(blocks_added) > 0) {
    detailed_changes <- bind_rows(detailed_changes,
      tibble(
        from_campaign = prev_camp,
        to_campaign = current_camp,
        change_type = "Block Added",
        element_id = blocks_added,
        parent_block = blocks_added,
        details = paste("New block added in", current_camp)
      ))
  }
  
  if(length(blocks_removed) > 0) {
    detailed_changes <- bind_rows(detailed_changes,
      tibble(
        from_campaign = prev_camp,
        to_campaign = current_camp,
        change_type = "Block Removed", 
        element_id = blocks_removed,
        parent_block = blocks_removed,
        details = paste("Block removed after", prev_camp)
      ))
  }
  
  if(length(parcels_added) > 0) {
    # Find which blocks these parcels belong to
    parcel_blocks <- data %>%
      filter(Camp == current_camp, Parcelle %in% parcels_added) %>%
      select(Parcelle, Bloc) %>%
      distinct()
    
    detailed_changes <- bind_rows(detailed_changes,
      parcel_blocks %>%
        transmute(
          from_campaign = prev_camp,
          to_campaign = current_camp,
          change_type = "Parcel Added",
          element_id = Parcelle,
          parent_block = Bloc,
          details = paste("New parcel added to block", Bloc, "in", current_camp)
        ))
  }
  
  if(length(parcels_removed) > 0) {
    # Find which blocks these parcels belonged to
    parcel_blocks <- data %>%
      filter(Camp == prev_camp, Parcelle %in% parcels_removed) %>%
      select(Parcelle, Bloc) %>%
      distinct()
    
    detailed_changes <- bind_rows(detailed_changes,
      parcel_blocks %>%
        transmute(
          from_campaign = prev_camp,
          to_campaign = current_camp,
          change_type = "Parcel Removed",
          element_id = Parcelle,
          parent_block = Bloc,
          details = paste("Parcel removed from block", Bloc, "after", prev_camp)
        ))
  }
}

# 3. Complete parcel tracking matrix
parcel_tracking_matrix <- data %>%
  select(Camp, Bloc, Parcelle) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  complete(Camp, nesting(Bloc, Parcelle), fill = list()) %>%
  mutate(present = !is.na(Camp)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Camp, values_from = present, values_fill = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(Bloc, Parcelle)

# Save all CSV files
if(!dir.exists("change_analysis_output")) dir.create("change_analysis_output")

write_csv(campaign_summary_detailed, "change_analysis_output/campaign_summary_detailed.csv")
write_csv(detailed_changes, "change_analysis_output/detailed_changes.csv") 
write_csv(parcel_tracking_matrix, "change_analysis_output/parcel_tracking_matrix.csv")

# Print summary
cat("\nCHANGE DETECTION SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================\n")
cat("Total campaigns analyzed:", nrow(campaign_summary_detailed), "\n")
cat("Total unique blocks:", length(unique(data$Bloc)), "\n")
cat("Total unique parcels:", length(unique(data$Parcelle)), "\n")
cat("Total changes detected:", nrow(detailed_changes), "\n")

# Display change summary table
cat("\nCHANGE TYPE SUMMARY:\n")
print(detailed_changes %>% 
        count(change_type) %>% 
        arrange(desc(n)))

print(combined_change_plots)
```

### I.2.1. Block-Parcel Structure heatmap

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# ENHANCED PLOT C: BLOCK-PARCEL STRUCTURE HEATMAP
# Publication-ready styling matching the first heatmap
# ============================================================================

# Set publication theme (matching the first document)
publication_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray95", size = 0.3),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA)
  )

# ENHANCED VISUALIZATION 3: Block-Parcel Structure Heatmap
block_parcel_heatmap_enhanced <- block_parcel_structure %>%
  mutate(
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2))),
    Bloc_ordered = factor(Bloc, levels = rev(sort(unique(block_parcel_structure$Bloc))))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Campaign_Year), y = Bloc_ordered, fill = n_parcels)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n_parcels > 0, n_parcels, "")), 
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Parcels per\nBlock", option = "plasma", 
                       trans = "sqrt", 
                       labels = function(x) ifelse(x == 0, "0", as.character(round(x)))) +
  labs(
    title = "Block-Parcel Structure Heatmap Across Campaigns",
    subtitle = "Number of parcels per block per campaign (numbers shown in each cell)",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Block ID",
    caption = "Numbers in cells show exact parcel counts; colors provide visual intensity reference"
  ) +
  publication_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 1, barheight = 8))

# Display the enhanced plot
print(block_parcel_heatmap_enhanced)

# Save the enhanced plot
ggsave("change_analysis_output/enhanced_block_parcel_heatmap.png", 
       block_parcel_heatmap_enhanced, 
       width = 16, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## I.3. Missing values analysis

```{r}
# Missing Values Analysis
cat("\n6. MISSING VALUES ANALYSIS\n")
cat("===========================\n")

# Overall missing values
missing_summary <- data %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  mutate(
    missing_percentage = round((missing_count / nrow(data)) * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

print("Missing values per variable:")
print(missing_summary)

# Variables with high missing values (>50%)
high_missing <- missing_summary %>%
  filter(missing_percentage > 50)

if(nrow(high_missing) > 0) {
  cat("\nVariables with >50% missing values:\n")
  print(high_missing)
} else {
  cat("\nNo variables with >50% missing values\n")
}
```

```{r}
# COMPREHENSIVE MISSING VALUES ANALYSIS
# =====================================

cat("\n6. COMPREHENSIVE MISSING VALUES ANALYSIS\n")
cat("==========================================\n")
library(VIM)  # For missing value visualizations
library(corrplot)  # For correlation plots

# Overall missing values summary
missing_summary <- data %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  mutate(
    missing_percentage = round((missing_count / nrow(data)) * 100, 2),
    complete_count = nrow(data) - missing_count,
    complete_percentage = round(100 - missing_percentage, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

print("Missing values per variable:")
print(missing_summary)

# Categorize variables by missing percentage
missing_categories <- missing_summary %>%
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      missing_percentage == 0 ~ "Complete (0%)",
      missing_percentage <= 10 ~ "Low Missing (1-10%)",
      missing_percentage <= 25 ~ "Moderate Missing (11-25%)",
      missing_percentage <= 50 ~ "High Missing (26-50%)",
      missing_percentage <= 75 ~ "Very High Missing (51-75%)",
      TRUE ~ "Mostly Missing (>75%)"
    ),
    category = factor(category, levels = c("Complete (0%)", "Low Missing (1-10%)", 
                                          "Moderate Missing (11-25%)", "High Missing (26-50%)",
                                          "Very High Missing (51-75%)", "Mostly Missing (>75%)"))
  )

cat("\nMissing value categories:\n")
print(table(missing_categories$category))

# Variables with high missing values (>50%)
high_missing <- missing_summary %>%
  filter(missing_percentage > 50)

if(nrow(high_missing) > 0) {
  cat("\nVariables with >50% missing values:\n")
  print(high_missing)
} else {
  cat("\nNo variables with >50% missing values\n")
}

# Missing patterns by campaign
missing_by_campaign <- data %>%
  group_by(Camp) %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Camp, names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_count") %>%
  left_join(
    data %>% count(Camp) %>% rename(total_obs = n),
    by = "Camp"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    missing_percentage = round((missing_count / total_obs) * 100, 2),
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))
  )

# Key variables for agricultural analysis
key_variables <- c("Brix_1er", "Pol_j_1er", "Fib_1er", "Tc.ha.real", "Pur_1er", 
                   "Surf", "Nb.ans", "Implantation", "Recolte_N", "Variete", 
                   "GAG", "Bloc", "Parcelle")

# Filter to key variables that exist in the data
existing_key_vars <- key_variables[key_variables %in% names(data)]

# =============================
# VISUALIZATION 1: Missing Values Overview
# =============================
plot_missing_overview <- missing_summary %>%
  head(20) %>%  # Top 20 variables with most missing values
  mutate(variable = reorder(variable, missing_count)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = missing_percentage)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = missing_percentage), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(missing_percentage, "%\n(", missing_count, ")")), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", name = "Missing %") +
  labs(
    title = "A. Missing Values Overview",
    subtitle = "Percentage and count of missing values per variable",
    x = "Variables",
    y = "Missing Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  coord_flip()

# =============================
# VISUALIZATION 2: Missing Values by Category
# =============================
plot_missing_categories <- missing_categories %>%
  count(category) %>%
  mutate(percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = category, y = n, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", percentage, "%)")), 
            vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E8B57", "#4682B4", "#DAA520", "#CD853F", "#9370DB", "#DC143C")) +
  labs(
    title = "B. Variables by Missing Value Categories",
    subtitle = "Distribution of variables across missing value ranges",
    x = "Missing Value Category",
    y = "Number of Variables"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# =============================
# VISUALIZATION 3: Missing Values Heatmap by Campaign
# =============================
if(length(existing_key_vars) > 0) {
  plot_missing_heatmap <- missing_by_campaign %>%
    filter(variable %in% existing_key_vars) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = factor(Campaign_Year), y = reorder(variable, missing_percentage), 
               fill = missing_percentage)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(missing_percentage > 0, 
                                paste0(missing_percentage, "%"), "")), 
              color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 2.5) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", name = "Missing %") +
    labs(
      title = "C. Missing Values Heatmap by Campaign",
      subtitle = "Missing percentage for key variables across campaigns",
      x = "Campaign Year",
      y = "Variables"
    ) +
    theme_nature() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
} else {
  plot_missing_heatmap <- ggplot() + 
    annotate("text", x = 1, y = 1, label = "No key variables found in dataset") +
    theme_void()
}

# =============================
# VISUALIZATION 4: Missing Value Patterns
# =============================
# Create a binary matrix for missing values (1 = missing, 0 = present)
missing_matrix <- data %>%
  select(all_of(existing_key_vars)) %>%
  is.na() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number()) %>%
  sample_n(min(1000, nrow(.))) %>%  # Sample for performance
  select(-row_id)

# Calculate missing combinations
missing_combinations <- missing_matrix %>%
  mutate(missing_pattern = apply(., 1, function(x) paste(as.numeric(x), collapse = ""))) %>%
  count(missing_pattern, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  mutate(
    missing_vars = map_chr(missing_pattern, function(pattern) {
      vars_missing <- existing_key_vars[as.logical(as.numeric(strsplit(pattern, "")[[1]]))]
      if(length(vars_missing) == 0) return("Complete cases")
      paste(vars_missing, collapse = ", ")
    })
  )

plot_missing_patterns <- missing_combinations %>%
  mutate(missing_vars = str_wrap(missing_vars, 30)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(missing_vars, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4682B4", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.1, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "D. Most Common Missing Value Patterns",
    subtitle = "Top 10 combinations of missing variables",
    x = "Missing Variable Combinations",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8)
  ) +
  coord_flip()

# =============================
# VISUALIZATION 5: Time Series of Missing Values
# =============================
missing_time_series <- missing_by_campaign %>%
  filter(variable %in% existing_key_vars[1:min(6, length(existing_key_vars))]) %>%  # Top 6 key variables
  ggplot(aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = missing_percentage, color = variable)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D", name = "Variables") +
  labs(
    title = "E. Missing Values Evolution Over Time",
    subtitle = "Trends in missing values for key variables across campaigns",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Missing Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# =============================
# VISUALIZATION 6: Completeness Score by Campaign
# =============================
campaign_completeness <- missing_by_campaign %>%
  filter(variable %in% existing_key_vars) %>%
  group_by(Camp, Campaign_Year) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_missing = mean(missing_percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
    completeness_score = 100 - avg_missing,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

plot_completeness <- campaign_completeness %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = completeness_score)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2E8B57", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "#2E8B57", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "#4682B4", alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) +
  labs(
    title = "F. Data Completeness Score by Campaign",
    subtitle = "Overall data quality trend (100% = complete, 0% = all missing)",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Completeness Score (%)"
  ) +
  theme_nature()

# =============================
# COMBINE ALL PLOTS
# =============================
combined_missing_plots <- (plot_missing_overview | plot_missing_categories) / 
                          (plot_missing_heatmap | plot_missing_patterns) /
                          (missing_time_series | plot_completeness) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Comprehensive Missing Values Analysis",
    subtitle = paste("Analysis of", nrow(data), "observations across", 
                     ncol(data), "variables"),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray60")
    )
  )

# Display the combined plot
print(combined_missing_plots)

# =============================
# CREATE DETAILED CSV OUTPUTS
# =============================

# 1. Variable-level missing summary
variable_missing_summary <- missing_summary %>%
  left_join(
    missing_categories %>% select(variable, category),
    by = "variable"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_percentage))

# 2. Campaign-level missing summary
campaign_missing_summary <- missing_by_campaign %>%
  filter(variable %in% existing_key_vars) %>%
  group_by(Camp, Campaign_Year) %>%
  summarise(
    variables_analyzed = n(),
    avg_missing_pct = round(mean(missing_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_missing_pct = round(max(missing_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    min_missing_pct = round(min(missing_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    variables_complete = sum(missing_percentage == 0),
    variables_with_missing = sum(missing_percentage > 0),
    completeness_score = round(100 - avg_missing_pct, 2),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# 3. Detailed missing patterns
detailed_missing_patterns <- missing_combinations %>%
  select(missing_pattern, missing_vars, n) %>%
  rename(frequency = n, variables_missing = missing_vars) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage_of_sample = round(frequency / sum(frequency) * 100, 2)
  )

# Save CSV files
if(!dir.exists("missing_analysis_output")) dir.create("missing_analysis_output")

write.csv(variable_missing_summary, "missing_analysis_output/variable_missing_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(campaign_missing_summary, "missing_analysis_output/campaign_missing_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(detailed_missing_patterns, "missing_analysis_output/missing_patterns.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# =============================
# PRINT COMPREHENSIVE SUMMARY
# =============================
cat("\nCOMPREHENSIVE MISSING VALUES SUMMARY\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat("Dataset dimensions:", nrow(data), "rows ×", ncol(data), "columns\n")
cat("Variables analyzed:", nrow(missing_summary), "\n")
cat("Complete variables (0% missing):", sum(missing_summary$missing_percentage == 0), "\n")
cat("Variables with some missing:", sum(missing_summary$missing_percentage > 0), "\n")
cat("Variables with >50% missing:", sum(missing_summary$missing_percentage > 50), "\n")

overall_completeness <- round(100 - mean(missing_summary$missing_percentage), 2)
cat("Overall dataset completeness:", overall_completeness, "%\n")

if(nrow(campaign_missing_summary) > 0) {
  best_campaign <- campaign_missing_summary$Camp[which.max(campaign_missing_summary$completeness_score)]
  worst_campaign <- campaign_missing_summary$Camp[which.min(campaign_missing_summary$completeness_score)]
  cat("Most complete campaign:", best_campaign, 
      "(", max(campaign_missing_summary$completeness_score, na.rm = TRUE), "% complete)\n")
  cat("Least complete campaign:", worst_campaign,
      "(", min(campaign_missing_summary$completeness_score, na.rm = TRUE), "% complete)\n")
}
print(combined_missing_plots)
```

## I.4. Date variables analysis

```{r}
# Date Variables Analysis
cat("\n7. DATE VARIABLES ANALYSIS\n")
cat("===========================\n")

# Identify date columns
date_columns <- c("Implantation", "Recolte_N", "Date R", "Date I", "Date_Sechage")
existing_date_cols <- intersect(date_columns, names(data))

if(length(existing_date_cols) > 0) {
  # Convert date columns
  data_dates <- data
  for(col in existing_date_cols) {
    data_dates[[col]] <- dmy(data_dates[[col]])
  }
  
  # Date ranges and patterns
  for(col in existing_date_cols) {
    cat("\n", col, ":\n")
    valid_dates <- data_dates[[col]][!is.na(data_dates[[col]])]
    if(length(valid_dates) > 0) {
      cat("  Range:", as.character(min(valid_dates)), "to", as.character(max(valid_dates)), "\n")
      cat("  Valid dates:", length(valid_dates), "/", nrow(data), "\n")
      cat("  Years covered:", paste(sort(unique(year(valid_dates))), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    } else {
      cat("  No valid dates found\n")
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("No date columns found in expected format\n")
}
```

## I.5. Timeline and coverage analysis

```{r}
# COMPREHENSIVE TIMELINE AND COVERAGE ANALYSIS
# ============================================

cat("\n7. COMPREHENSIVE DATE VARIABLES AND TIMELINE ANALYSIS\n")
cat("=====================================================\n")

# Identify and process date columns
date_columns <- c("Implantation", "Recolte_N", "Date R", "Date I", "Date_Sechage")
existing_date_cols <- intersect(date_columns, names(data))

cat("Available date columns:", paste(existing_date_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")

if(length(existing_date_cols) > 0) {
  # Convert date columns and create enhanced dataset
  data_dates <- data
  for(col in existing_date_cols) {
    data_dates[[col]] <- dmy(data_dates[[col]])
  }
  
  # Add campaign year information
  data_dates <- data_dates %>%
    mutate(
      Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2))),
      Campaign_End_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 4, 5)))
    )
  
  # Basic date ranges and patterns
  date_summary <- tibble()
  for(col in existing_date_cols) {
    valid_dates <- data_dates[[col]][!is.na(data_dates[[col]])]
    if(length(valid_dates) > 0) {
      date_summary <- bind_rows(date_summary, 
        tibble(
          date_variable = col,
          min_date = min(valid_dates),
          max_date = max(valid_dates),
          valid_count = length(valid_dates),
          total_count = nrow(data),
          coverage_pct = round((length(valid_dates) / nrow(data)) * 100, 2),
          years_span = max(year(valid_dates)) - min(year(valid_dates)) + 1,
          unique_years = paste(sort(unique(year(valid_dates))), collapse = ", ")
        ))
      
      cat("\n", col, ":\n")
      cat("  Range:", as.character(min(valid_dates)), "to", as.character(max(valid_dates)), "\n")
      cat("  Valid dates:", length(valid_dates), "/", nrow(data), 
          "(", round((length(valid_dates) / nrow(data)) * 100, 1), "%)\n")
      cat("  Years covered:", paste(sort(unique(year(valid_dates))), collapse = ", "), "\n")
      cat("  Time span:", max(year(valid_dates)) - min(year(valid_dates)) + 1, "years\n")
    } else {
      cat("\n", col, ": No valid dates found\n")
    }
  }
  
  print("Date Variables Summary:")
  print(date_summary)
  
  # =============================
  # ENHANCED TIMELINE ANALYSIS
  # =============================
  
  # Create comprehensive timeline data
  timeline_data <- data_dates %>%
    select(Camp, Campaign_Year, all_of(existing_date_cols), Bloc, Parcelle) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(existing_date_cols), 
                 names_to = "date_type", values_to = "date_value") %>%
    filter(!is.na(date_value)) %>%
    mutate(
      year = year(date_value),
      month = month(date_value),
      day_of_year = yday(date_value),
      season = case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Dry Season",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Hot Dry",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8, 9) ~ "Rainy Season",
        month %in% c(10, 11) ~ "Post-Rainy",
        TRUE ~ "Unknown"
      ),
      month_name = month.abb[month]
    )
  
  # Campaign coverage analysis
  campaign_coverage <- data_dates %>%
    group_by(Camp, Campaign_Year) %>%
    summarise(
      total_observations = n(),
      n_blocks = n_distinct(Bloc, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_parcels = n_distinct(Parcelle, na.rm = TRUE),
      across(all_of(existing_date_cols), ~sum(!is.na(.)), .names = "valid_{.col}"),
      across(all_of(existing_date_cols), ~round(sum(!is.na(.)) / n() * 100, 1), .names = "pct_{.col}"),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  # =============================
  # VISUALIZATION 1: Dataset Timeline Overview
  # =============================
  dataset_timeline <- data_dates %>%
    group_by(Campaign_Year) %>%
    summarise(
      observations = n(),
      blocks = n_distinct(Bloc, na.rm = TRUE),
      parcels = n_distinct(Parcelle, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  plot_timeline_overview <- dataset_timeline %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Campaign_Year)) +
    geom_col(aes(y = observations), fill = "#2E8B57", alpha = 0.7, width = 0.8) +
    geom_line(aes(y = blocks * 20), color = "#4682B4", size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(y = blocks * 20), color = "#4682B4", size = 3) +
    geom_line(aes(y = parcels * 5), color = "#CD853F", size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(y = parcels * 5), color = "#CD853F", size = 3) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "Observations",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(trans = ~./20, name = "Blocks / (Parcels ÷ 4)")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "A. Dataset Timeline and Sampling Coverage",
      subtitle = "Green bars: observations | Blue line: blocks | Brown line: parcels (÷4)",
      x = "Campaign Year"
    ) +
    theme_nature() +
    theme(
      axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "#4682B4"),
      axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "#4682B4")
    )
  
  # =============================
  # VISUALIZATION 2: Date Variable Coverage Heatmap
  # =============================
  coverage_heatmap_data <- campaign_coverage %>%
    select(Campaign_Year, starts_with("pct_")) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
                 names_to = "date_variable", values_to = "coverage_pct") %>%
    mutate(
      date_variable = str_remove(date_variable, "pct_"),
      date_variable = case_when(
        date_variable == "Implantation" ~ "Planting Date",
        date_variable == "Recolte_N" ~ "Harvest Date",
        date_variable == "Date_R" ~ "R Date",
        date_variable == "Date_I" ~ "I Date",
        date_variable == "Date_Sechage" ~ "Drying Date",
        TRUE ~ date_variable
      )
    )
  
  plot_coverage_heatmap <- coverage_heatmap_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = factor(Campaign_Year), y = reorder(date_variable, coverage_pct), 
               fill = coverage_pct)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(coverage_pct, "%")), 
              color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", name = "Coverage %") +
    labs(
      title = "B. Date Variable Coverage by Campaign",
      subtitle = "Percentage of observations with valid dates",
      x = "Campaign Year",
      y = "Date Variables"
    ) +
    theme_nature() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
  
  # =============================
  # VISUALIZATION 3: Seasonal Distribution of Activities
  # =============================
  if(nrow(timeline_data) > 0) {
    seasonal_activities <- timeline_data %>%
      filter(date_type %in% c("Implantation", "Recolte_N")) %>%
      count(date_type, season, month_name, month) %>%
      arrange(month) %>%
      mutate(
        date_type = case_when(
          date_type == "Implantation" ~ "Planting",
          date_type == "Recolte_N" ~ "Harvest",
          TRUE ~ date_type
        ),
        month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month.abb)
      )
    
    plot_seasonal_distribution <- seasonal_activities %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = month_name, y = n, fill = date_type)) +
      geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7) +
      facet_wrap(~season, scales = "free_x") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("Planting" = "#2E8B57", "Harvest" = "#CD853F")) +
      labs(
        title = "C. Seasonal Distribution of Agricultural Activities",
        subtitle = "Monthly patterns of planting and harvest dates",
        x = "Month",
        y = "Number of Activities",
        fill = "Activity Type"
      ) +
      theme_nature() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95")
      )
  } else {
    plot_seasonal_distribution <- ggplot() + 
      annotate("text", x = 1, y = 1, label = "No seasonal data available") +
      theme_void()
  }
  
  # =============================
  # VISUALIZATION 4: Data Quality Evolution
  # =============================
  quality_evolution <- campaign_coverage %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      avg_coverage = mean(c_across(starts_with("pct_")), na.rm = TRUE),
      data_quality_score = case_when(
        avg_coverage >= 90 ~ "Excellent (≥90%)",
        avg_coverage >= 75 ~ "Good (75-89%)",
        avg_coverage >= 50 ~ "Fair (50-74%)",
        TRUE ~ "Poor (<50%)"
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  plot_quality_evolution <- quality_evolution %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Campaign_Year, y = avg_coverage)) +
    geom_line(color = "#2E8B57", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(color = data_quality_score), size = 4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, color = "#4682B4") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Excellent (≥90%)" = "#2E8B57", 
                                 "Good (75-89%)" = "#4682B4",
                                 "Fair (50-74%)" = "#DAA520", 
                                 "Poor (<50%)" = "#CD853F")) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    labs(
      title = "D. Data Quality Evolution Over Time",
      subtitle = "Average coverage of date variables across campaigns",
      x = "Campaign Year",
      y = "Average Coverage (%)",
      color = "Quality Level"
    ) +
    theme_nature()
  
  # =============================
  # VISUALIZATION 5: Timeline Gantt Chart
  # =============================
  if("Implantation" %in% existing_date_cols && "Recolte_N" %in% existing_date_cols) {
    gantt_data <- data_dates %>%
      filter(!is.na(Implantation) & !is.na(Recolte_N)) %>%
      mutate(
        crop_duration = as.numeric(Recolte_N - Implantation),
        campaign_label = paste("Campaign", Camp)
      ) %>%
      filter(crop_duration > 0 & crop_duration < 500) %>%  # Remove outliers
      sample_n(min(50, nrow(.)))  # Sample for visualization clarity
    
    plot_gantt <- gantt_data %>%
      ggplot(aes(y = reorder(campaign_label, Campaign_Year))) +
      geom_segment(aes(x = Implantation, xend = Recolte_N, color = crop_duration), 
                   size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_point(aes(x = Implantation), color = "#2E8B57", size = 2) +
      geom_point(aes(x = Recolte_N), color = "#CD853F", size = 2) +
      scale_color_viridis_c(option = "D", name = "Duration\n(days)") +
      labs(
        title = "E. Crop Cycle Timeline (Sample)",
        subtitle = "Green dots: planting | Brown dots: harvest | Lines: crop duration",
        x = "Date",
        y = "Campaign"
      ) +
      theme_nature() +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
  } else {
    plot_gantt <- ggplot() + 
      annotate("text", x = 1, y = 1, label = "Planting/Harvest data not available") +
      theme_void()
  }
  
  # =============================
  # VISUALIZATION 6: Coverage Summary Dashboard
  # =============================
  coverage_summary <- date_summary %>%
    mutate(
      quality_level = case_when(
        coverage_pct >= 90 ~ "Excellent",
        coverage_pct >= 75 ~ "Good", 
        coverage_pct >= 50 ~ "Fair",
        TRUE ~ "Poor"
      )
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(date_variable, coverage_pct), y = coverage_pct)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = quality_level), alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(coverage_pct, "%\n(", valid_count, "/", total_count, ")")), 
              hjust = -0.1, fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Excellent" = "#2E8B57", "Good" = "#4682B4",
                                "Fair" = "#DAA520", "Poor" = "#CD853F")) +
    labs(
      title = "F. Date Variables Coverage Summary",
      subtitle = "Overall data availability across all campaigns",
      x = "Date Variables",
      y = "Coverage Percentage (%)",
      fill = "Quality Level"
    ) +
    theme_nature() +
    coord_flip()
  
  # =============================
  # COMBINE ALL PLOTS
  # =============================
  combined_timeline_plots <- (plot_timeline_overview | plot_coverage_heatmap) / 
                            (plot_seasonal_distribution | plot_quality_evolution) /
                            (plot_gantt | coverage_summary) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Comprehensive Timeline and Coverage Analysis",
      subtitle = paste("Agricultural dataset spanning", 
                       min(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE), "-",
                       max(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE),
                       "with", nrow(data), "total observations"),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "gray60")
      )
    )
  
  # Display the plot
  print(combined_timeline_plots)
  
  # =============================
  # CREATE CSV OUTPUTS
  # =============================
  
  # 1. Date variables summary
  date_variables_summary <- date_summary %>%
    mutate(
      data_quality = case_when(
        coverage_pct >= 90 ~ "Excellent",
        coverage_pct >= 75 ~ "Good",
        coverage_pct >= 50 ~ "Fair", 
        TRUE ~ "Poor"
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(coverage_pct))
  
  # 2. Campaign timeline summary
  campaign_timeline_summary <- campaign_coverage %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      avg_date_coverage = round(mean(c_across(starts_with("pct_")), na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      min_date_coverage = min(c_across(starts_with("pct_")), na.rm = TRUE),
      max_date_coverage = max(c_across(starts_with("pct_")), na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(Campaign_Year)
  
  # 3. Overall dataset timeline info
  overall_timeline <- tibble(
    dataset_name = "Agricultural Dataset",
    first_campaign = min(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_campaign = max(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_years = max(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE) - min(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE) + 1,
    total_campaigns = n_distinct(data$Camp),
    total_observations = nrow(data),
    unique_blocks = n_distinct(data$Bloc, na.rm = TRUE),
    unique_parcels = n_distinct(data$Parcelle, na.rm = TRUE),
    date_variables_available = length(existing_date_cols),
    overall_date_coverage = round(mean(date_summary$coverage_pct), 2),
    data_collection_span = paste(min(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                max(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE), sep = "-"),
    primary_use = "Agricultural performance analysis baseline"
  )
  
  # Save CSV files
  if(!dir.exists("timeline_analysis_output")) dir.create("timeline_analysis_output")
  
  write.csv(date_variables_summary, "timeline_analysis_output/date_variables_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(campaign_timeline_summary, "timeline_analysis_output/campaign_timeline_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(overall_timeline, "timeline_analysis_output/overall_timeline.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  
  # =============================
  # FINAL SUMMARY REPORT
  # =============================
  cat("\n", "="*60, "\n")
  cat("COMPREHENSIVE TIMELINE ANALYSIS SUMMARY\n")
  cat("="*60, "\n")
  cat("DATASET SCOPE:\n")
  cat("• Time Range:", min(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE), "-", 
      max(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE), "(", 
      max(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE) - min(data_dates$Campaign_Year, na.rm = TRUE) + 1, "years)\n")
  cat("• Total Campaigns:", n_distinct(data$Camp), "\n")
  cat("• Total Observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
  cat("• Sampling Units:", n_distinct(data$Bloc, na.rm = TRUE), "blocks,", 
      n_distinct(data$Parcelle, na.rm = TRUE), "parcels\n")
  
  cat("\nDATE VARIABLES PERFORMANCE:\n")
  for(i in 1:nrow(date_summary)) {
    cat("•", date_summary$date_variable[i], ":", date_summary$coverage_pct[i], 
        "% coverage (", date_summary$valid_count[i], "/", date_summary$total_count[i], ")\n")
  }
  
  best_coverage <- date_summary$date_variable[which.max(date_summary$coverage_pct)]
  worst_coverage <- date_summary$date_variable[which.min(date_summary$coverage_pct)]

  
```

## I.6. Data visualization by ggplot2

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)
library(ggridges)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(scales)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(cowplot)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggsignif)
library(ggtext)


# Data preparation
data_clean <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert campaign to proper format and create year
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2))),
    Campaign_End_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 4, 5))),
    Campaign_Period = factor(Camp),
    
    # Convert dates
    Implantation_Date = dmy(Implantation),
    Harvest_Date = dmy(Recolte_N),
    
    # Create season from implantation date - Sahel Climate
    Implantation_Month = month(Implantation_Date),
    Season = case_when(
      Implantation_Month %in% c(6, 7, 8, 9, 10) ~ "Wet Season",
      Implantation_Month %in% c(11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) ~ "Dry Season",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    
    # Clean numerical variables
    Sugar_Content_Brix = as.numeric(`Brix_1er`),
    Pol_Content = as.numeric(`Pol_j_1er`),
    Fiber_Content = as.numeric(`Fib_1er`),
    Tonnage_per_Ha = as.numeric(Tc.ha.real),
    Purity = as.numeric(`Pur_1er`),
    Surface_Area = as.numeric(Surf),
    
    # Create productivity categories
    Productivity_Category = case_when(
      Tonnage_per_Ha >= quantile(Tonnage_per_Ha, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High",
      Tonnage_per_Ha >= quantile(Tonnage_per_Ha, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Medium",
      TRUE ~ "Low"
    ),
    
    # Extract irrigation info from GAG - Updated for Sahel conditions
    Irrigation_Type = case_when(
      str_detect(GAG, "GAG") ~ "Drip",
      str_detect(GAG, "GRV") ~ "Gravity",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    
    # Age categories
    Age_Category = case_when(
      Nb.ans <= 2 ~ "Young (≤2 years)",
      Nb.ans <= 4 ~ "Mature (3-4 years)",
      Nb.ans > 4 ~ "Old (>4 years)",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Campaign_Year))

# Set theme for Nature-style publications
theme_nature <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey40", hjust = 0),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.3),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey98", color = "grey90")
    )
}

# Set the theme globally
theme_set(theme_nature())

# Color palettes
nature_colors <- c("#2E8B57", "#4682B4", "#DAA520", "#CD853F", "#9370DB")
viridis_discrete <- scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9)
viridis_continuous <- scale_color_viridis_c(option = "D", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9)

# Plot 1: Temporal Evolution of Key Parameters with Trend Analysis
cat("Creating Plot 1: Temporal Evolution Analysis...\n")

# Prepare data for temporal analysis
# Prepare data for temporal analysis
temporal_data <- data_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(Sugar_Content_Brix) & !is.na(Tonnage_per_Ha) & !is.na(Fiber_Content)) %>%
  group_by(Campaign_Year, Irrigation_Type) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Sugar = mean(Sugar_Content_Brix, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Tonnage = mean(Tonnage_per_Ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Fiber = mean(Fiber_Content, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Sugar = sd(Sugar_Content_Brix, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Tonnage = sd(Tonnage_per_Ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Fiber = sd(Fiber_Content, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Fix the standard error calculation
  mutate(
    SE_Sugar = ifelse(n_obs > 1, SD_Sugar / sqrt(n_obs), 0),
    SE_Tonnage = ifelse(n_obs > 1, SD_Tonnage / sqrt(n_obs), 0),
    SE_Fiber = ifelse(n_obs > 1, SD_Fiber / sqrt(n_obs), 0)
  ) %>%
  filter(n_obs >= 3)

# Prepare combined data for overall trend
combined_temporal_data <- data_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(Sugar_Content_Brix) & !is.na(Tonnage_per_Ha) & !is.na(Fiber_Content)) %>%
  group_by(Campaign_Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Sugar_Combined = mean(Sugar_Content_Brix, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Tonnage_Combined = mean(Tonnage_per_Ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  filter(n_obs >= 5)

unique(data_clean$GAG)
unique(data_clean$Variete)
```

```{r}
      TRUE ~ Parameter

    y = "Age Category"

  theme(
```

```{r}
      str_detect(Variety_Raw, "^SP\\s*71\\s*1081") ~ "SP 711081",
      str_detect(Variety_Raw, "^SP\\s*75\\s*184") ~ "SP 75184",
      str_detect(Variety_Raw, "^FR\\s*8783") ~ "FR 8783",
```

```{r}
# Safe function to clean character data
safe_clean_chars <- function(x) {
  if (!is.character(x)) return(x)
  
  # Remove NA first
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  
  # Remove empty strings
  x <- x[x != ""]
  
  # Handle encoding issues safely
  valid_data <- c()
  for (item in x) {
    tryCatch({
      # Try to process the string
      if (is.character(item) && !is.na(item)) {
        # Convert encoding if needed
        item_clean <- iconv(item, to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
        if (!is.na(item_clean) && item_clean != "") {
          valid_data <- c(valid_data, item_clean)
        }
      }
    }, error = function(e) {
      # Skip problematic strings
    })
  }
  
  return(valid_data)
}

# Main extraction function
extract_samples_safe <- function(data, n_samples = 5) {
  
  results <- list()
  
  for (i in 1:ncol(data)) {
    col_name <- names(data)[i]
    col_data <- data[[i]]
    
    cat("Processing variable", i, ":", col_name, "\n")
    
    # Handle different data types
    if (is.character(col_data) || is.factor(col_data)) {
      # Convert factors to character
      if (is.factor(col_data)) {
        col_data <- as.character(col_data)
      }
      
      # Clean character data safely
      clean_data <- safe_clean_chars(col_data)
      
    } else {
      # For numeric, date, logical data
      clean_data <- col_data[!is.na(col_data)]
    }
    
    # Get samples
    if (length(clean_data) > 0) {
      unique_vals <- unique(clean_data)
      
      if (length(unique_vals) <= n_samples) {
        sample_vals <- unique_vals
      } else {
        sample_vals <- sample(unique_vals, n_samples)
      }
      
      results[[col_name]] <- list(
        variable = col_name,
        samples = sample_vals,
        total_count = length(clean_data),
        unique_count = length(unique_vals),
        data_type = class(col_data)[1]
      )
    } else {
      results[[col_name]] <- list(
        variable = col_name,
        samples = "No valid data",
        total_count = 0,
        unique_count = 0,
        data_type = class(col_data)[1]
      )
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# Extract samples
cat("Starting sample extraction...\n")
samples_results <- extract_samples_safe(data, n_samples = 5)

# Display results
cat("\n=== SAMPLE RESULTS ===\n")
for (var_name in names(samples_results)) {
  result <- samples_results[[var_name]]
  cat("\nVariable:", result$variable)
  cat("\nType:", result$data_type)
  cat("\nTotal values:", result$total_count)
  cat("\nUnique values:", result$unique_count)
  
  if (result$total_count > 0) {
    cat("\nSample values:", paste(result$samples, collapse = " | "))
  } else {
    cat("\nSample values: No valid data")
  }
  cat("\n", rep("-", 50), "\n")
}

# Create a simple summary table
summary_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  Type = character(),
  Total = numeric(),
  Unique = numeric(),
  Sample1 = character(),
  Sample2 = character(),
  Sample3 = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (var_name in names(samples_results)) {
  result <- samples_results[[var_name]]
  samples <- result$samples
  
  if (length(samples) == 1 && samples == "No valid data") {
    samples <- c(NA, NA, NA)
  } else {
    # Pad with NA if fewer than 3 samples
    samples <- c(samples, rep(NA, 3 - length(samples)))[1:3]
  }
  
  summary_df <- rbind(summary_df, data.frame(
    Variable = result$variable,
    Type = result$data_type,
    Total = result$total_count,
    Unique = result$unique_count,
    Sample1 = ifelse(is.na(samples[1]), "", as.character(samples[1])),
    Sample2 = ifelse(is.na(samples[2]), "", as.character(samples[2])),
    Sample3 = ifelse(is.na(samples[3]), "", as.character(samples[3])),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# Show summary table
cat("\n=== SUMMARY TABLE ===\n")
print(summary_df)

# Save results
write.csv(summary_df, "sugarcane_samples.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nResults saved to 'sugarcane_samples.csv'\n")

# Quick check for key variables
cat("\n=== KEY VARIABLES QUICK CHECK ===\n")
key_vars <- c("variety", "irrigation_type", "tc_per_ha_actual", "brix_percent", "farm")

for (var in key_vars) {
  if (var %in% names(samples_results)) {
    result <- samples_results[[var]]
    cat(var, ":", result$unique_count, "unique values,", result$total_count, "total values\n")
    if (result$total_count > 0) {
      cat("  Samples:", paste(head(result$samples, 3), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    }
  }
}
```

### I.7.1. Data type conversion

```{r}
# Data Type Conversion Script for Sugarcane Dataset
# Load required libraries
library(lubridate)

# Function to safely convert to numeric, handling commas and special values
safe_numeric <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(numeric(0))
  # Replace commas with dots for decimal places
  x <- gsub(",", ".", x)
  # Handle special Excel values
  x[x %in% c("#N/A", "#VALEUR!", "#NULL!", "#DIV/0!", "", "NA")] <- NA
  # Convert to numeric
  as.numeric(x)
}

# Function to safely convert dates, handling multiple formats
safe_date <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(as.Date(character(0)))
  # Handle special Excel values
  x[x %in% c("#N/A", "#VALEUR!", "#NULL!", "#DIV/0!", "", "NA")] <- NA
  
  # Try multiple date formats
  dates <- as.Date(x, format = "%d/%m/%Y")
  
  # For any that didn't convert, try other common formats
  failed_indices <- is.na(dates) & !is.na(x)
  if (any(failed_indices)) {
    # Try other formats
    dates[failed_indices] <- as.Date(x[failed_indices], format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  }
  
  # For numeric dates (Excel serial dates)
  still_failed <- is.na(dates) & !is.na(x)
  if (any(still_failed)) {
    numeric_dates <- as.numeric(x[still_failed])
    if (any(!is.na(numeric_dates))) {
      # Excel dates start from 1900-01-01 (but Excel thinks 1900 was a leap year)
      dates[still_failed][!is.na(numeric_dates)] <- 
        as.Date("1899-12-30") + numeric_dates[!is.na(numeric_dates)]
    }
  }
  
  return(dates)
}

# Function to safely convert to factor, handling special values
safe_factor <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return(factor(character(0)))
  # Handle special Excel values
  x[x %in% c("#N/A", "#VALEUR!", "#NULL!", "#DIV/0!", "", "NA")] <- NA
  as.factor(x)
}

# Function to safely convert columns with existence check
safe_convert_column <- function(data, col_name, conversion_func, var_type = "unknown") {
  if (col_name %in% names(data)) {
    tryCatch({
      data[[col_name]] <- conversion_func(data[[col_name]])
      cat("✓ Converted", col_name, "to", var_type, "\n")
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("✗ Error converting", col_name, ":", e$message, "\n")
    })
  } else {
    cat("⚠ Column", col_name, "not found in dataset\n")
  }
  return(data)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to detect outliers using IQR method
detect_outliers <- function(x) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
}

# Function to add line breaks to long labels
format_labels <- function(labels, max_length = 12) {
  sapply(labels, function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x)
    if (is.na(x) || x == "NA") {
      return(x)
    }
    
    if (nchar(x) > max_length) {
      words <- strsplit(x, "[ _()]")[[1]]
      words <- words[words != ""]
      
      if (length(words) > 1) {
        mid_point <- ceiling(length(words) / 2)
        first_part <- words[1:min(mid_point, length(words))]
        second_part <- words[max(1, mid_point + 1):length(words)]
        
        first_part <- first_part[!is.na(first_part)]
        second_part <- second_part[!is.na(second_part)]
        
        if (length(first_part) > 0 && length(second_part) > 0) {
          paste(paste(first_part, collapse = " "), 
                paste(second_part, collapse = " "), sep = "\n")
        } else {
          x
        }
      } else {
        if (nchar(x) > max_length * 1.5) {
          mid_char <- ceiling(nchar(x) / 2)
          paste(substr(x, 1, mid_char), substr(x, mid_char + 1, nchar(x)), sep = "\n")
        } else {
          x
        }
      }
    } else {
      x
    }
  }, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# Enhanced function to create narrow boxplots with red outlier detection
create_enhanced_boxplot <- function(data_long, title, subtitle, colors, x_label, y_label, 
                                  variable_col = "variable", value_col = "value", remove_outliers = FALSE) {
  
  # Detect outliers for each variable
  data_with_outliers <- data_long %>%
    group_by(!!sym(variable_col)) %>%
    mutate(
      is_outlier = detect_outliers(!!sym(value_col)),
      outlier_label = ifelse(is_outlier, "Outlier", "Normal")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Remove outliers if requested
  if (remove_outliers) {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers %>% filter(!is_outlier)
    title <- paste(title, "(Without Outliers)")
  } else {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers
  }
  
  # Format labels for better display
  plot_data[[variable_col]] <- format_labels(plot_data[[variable_col]])
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col, fill = variable_col)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      alpha = 0.85, 
      outlier.shape = NA,
      width = 0.18,
      color = "#000000",
      size = 0.6,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # Add red outlier points manually
    {if (!remove_outliers) {
      geom_point(
        data = plot_data %>% filter(is_outlier),
        aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col),
        color = "#DC143C",
        size = 1.2,
        alpha = 0.8,
        shape = 16,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
    }} +
    stat_summary(
      fun = median, 
      geom = "text", 
      aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", after_stat(y))),
      size = 2.2,
      color = "white", 
      fontface = "bold",
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    publication_theme +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
  
  return(p)
}

cat("Creating Campaign Evolution analysis...\n")

# Clean campaign data and convert to proper time format
campaign_data <- sugarcane_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(campaign)) %>%
  mutate(
    campaign_clean = as.character(campaign),
    # Extract years from campaign format (e.g., "03-04" becomes 2003-2004)
    start_year = case_when(
      str_detect(campaign_clean, "^\\d{2}-\\d{2}$") ~ 
        paste0("20", str_sub(campaign_clean, 1, 2)),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    campaign_numeric = as.numeric(start_year)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(campaign_numeric))

# Yield evolution by campaign
if(nrow(campaign_data) > 0) {
  yield_evolution <- campaign_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(tc_per_ha_actual)) %>%
    group_by(campaign_clean, campaign_numeric) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_yield = mean(tc_per_ha_actual, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_yield = median(tc_per_ha_actual, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_samples = n(),
      sd_yield = sd(tc_per_ha_actual, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    filter(n_samples >= 3) %>%
    arrange(campaign_numeric)
  
  if(nrow(yield_evolution) > 3) {
    p10_yield_evolution <- ggplot(yield_evolution, aes(x = campaign_numeric)) +
      geom_line(aes(y = mean_yield), color = "#228B22", size = 1.2) +
      geom_point(aes(y = mean_yield, size = n_samples), color = "#228B22", alpha = 0.8) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_yield - sd_yield/sqrt(n_samples), 
                       ymax = mean_yield + sd_yield/sqrt(n_samples)),
                   color = "#228B22", alpha = 0.6, width = 0.2) +
      geom_smooth(aes(y = mean_yield), method = "loess", se = TRUE, 
                 color = "#2F4F4F", fill = "#87CEEB", alpha = 0.3) +
      labs(
        title = "Yield Evolution Across Campaigns",
        subtitle = "Mean TC per hectare over time (error bars = standard error)",
        x = "Campaign Year (Start)",
        y = "Mean TC per ha",
        size = "Samples"
      ) +
      publication_theme +
      theme(legend.position = "right") +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2003, 2024, 3))
    
    ggsave("Sugarcane_Analysis_Publication/10_Yield_Evolution_Campaigns.png", p10_yield_evolution,
           width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# 10. COMPREHENSIVE CORRELATION MATRIX
# ============================================================================
cat("Creating comprehensive correlation matrix...\n")

# Select key numeric variables for correlation analysis
key_variables <- sugarcane_data %>%
  select(tc_per_ha_actual, tc_per_ha_per_week, brix_percent, pol_juice_percent,
         purity_percent, fiber_percent, age_years, age_weeks, surface_area_ha,
         hugot_sugar, glucose_cane_percent, percent_cane_percent, tons_per_ha,
         tons_per_ha_per_week, ts, tsr, tmss, juice_tons) %>%
  # Convert all columns to numeric
  mutate_all(~as.numeric(as.character(.))) %>%
  # Keep only variables with at least 10 non-NA values
  select_if(~sum(!is.na(.)) > 10) %>%
  # Remove rows with too many NAs
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(.)) >= 5)

# Only proceed if we have enough data
if(ncol(key_variables) >= 3 && nrow(key_variables) >= 10) {
  
  tryCatch({
    cor_result <- rcorr(as.matrix(key_variables), type = "pearson")
    cor_matrix <- cor_result$r
    p_matrix <- cor_result$P
    
    # Clean correlation matrix
    cor_matrix[is.na(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    cor_matrix[is.infinite(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    diag(cor_matrix) <- 1
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Hmisc method failed, using base R correlation...\n")
    cor_matrix <- cor(key_variables, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
    cor_matrix[is.na(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    cor_matrix[is.infinite(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    diag(cor_matrix) <- 1
    p_matrix <- NULL
  })
  
  # Create enhanced correlation plot
  png("Sugarcane_Analysis_Publication/13_Comprehensive_Correlation_Matrix.png", 
      width = 11, height = 9, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
  
  par(mar = c(2, 2, 4, 2))
  
  corr_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", 
                                   "#D1E5F0", "#F7F7F7", 
                                   "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B", "#67001F"))(100)
  
  corrplot(cor_matrix,
           method = "color",
           type = "upper",
           order = "hclust",
           col = corr_colors,
           tl.col = "#000000",
           tl.srt = 45,
           tl.cex = 0.8,
           tl.font = 2,
           cl.cex = 1.0,
           title = "Correlation Matrix of Key Sugarcane Variables\n(Pearson Correlation Coefficients)",
           mar = c(0,0,3,0),
           diag = FALSE,
           addCoef.col = "#000000",
           number.cex = 0.5,
           number.digits = 2,
           number.font = 1,
           outline = TRUE,
           cl.ratio = 0.15)
  
  # Add significance stars if p_matrix is available
  if(!is.null(p_matrix)) {
    n_vars <- ncol(cor_matrix)
    for(i in 1:(n_vars-1)) {
      for(j in (i+1):n_vars) {
        if(!is.na(p_matrix[i,j])) {
          if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.001) {
            sig_symbol <- "***"
          } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.01) {
            sig_symbol <- "**"
          } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.05) {
            sig_symbol <- "*"
          } else {
            sig_symbol <- ""
          }
          
          if(sig_symbol != "" && !is.na(cor_matrix[i,j]) && abs(cor_matrix[i,j]) > 0.1) {
            x_center <- j
            y_center <- n_vars - i + 1
            text(x_center, y_center + 0.25, sig_symbol, 
                 cex = 0.6, col = "#000000", font = 2)
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  
  
  
  dev.off()
}

# Enhanced function to create histogram with normal overlay
create_histogram <- function(data, variable, title, color, x_label) {
  
  data_clean_values <- as.numeric(as.character(data[[variable]]))
  data_clean_values <- data_clean_values[!is.na(data_clean_values)]
  
  if(length(data_clean_values) < 10) {
    cat("Insufficient data for", variable, "histogram\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  plot_data <- data.frame(values = data_clean_values)
  
  mean_val <- mean(data_clean_values)
  sd_val <- sd(data_clean_values)
  min_val <- min(data_clean_values)
  max_val <- max(data_clean_values)
  
  n_bins <- min(30, max(10, length(data_clean_values) / 10))
  bin_width <- (max_val - min_val) / n_bins
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = values)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = n_bins, fill = color, color = "#000000", alpha = 0.7, boundary = 0) +
    geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(density) * length(data_clean_values) * bin_width),
                color = "#DC143C", size = 1.2) +
    stat_function(fun = function(x) dnorm(x, mean = mean_val, sd = sd_val) * 
                  length(data_clean_values) * bin_width,
                  color = "#2F4F4F", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = "Red: actual density, Dashed: normal distribution",
      x = x_label,
      y = "Frequency"
    ) +
    publication_theme +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 12)),
      axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 12)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 12))
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 1))
  
  return(p)
}

# Create histograms for key variables

# Outlier analysis function
calculate_outlier_stats <- function(data, variable_name) {
  x <- data[[variable_name]]
  x_clean <- x[!is.na(x)]
  
  if(length(x_clean) < 10) return(NULL)
  
  q1 <- quantile(x_clean, 0.25)
  q3 <- quantile(x_clean, 0.75)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  
  outliers <- x_clean[x_clean < lower_bound | x_clean > upper_bound]
  
  data.frame(
    Variable = variable_name,
    Total_Observations = length(x_clean),
    Number_of_Outliers = length(outliers),
    Outlier_Percentage = round((length(outliers) / length(x_clean)) * 100, 2),
    Q1 = round(q1, 3),
    Q3 = round(q3, 3),
    IQR = round(iqr, 3),
    Lower_Bound = round(lower_bound, 3),
    Upper_Bound = round(upper_bound, 3),
    Min_Outlier = ifelse(length(outliers) > 0, round(min(outliers), 3), NA),
    Max_Outlier = ifelse(length(outliers) > 0, round(max(outliers), 3), NA)
  )
}

# Calculate outlier statistics for key variables
key_vars <- c("tc_per_ha_actual", "brix_percent", "pol_juice_percent", "purity_percent",
              "fiber_percent", "age_years", "surface_area_ha", "hugot_sugar")

outlier_analysis <- map_dfr(key_vars, ~calculate_outlier_stats(sugarcane_data, .x)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Variable)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Outlier_Percentage))

# Save outlier analysis

# Generate final report
final_report <- list(

  )
)

# Save final report as JSON
library(jsonlite)
```

## I.8.1. Comprehensive correlation matrix

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# 10. COMPREHENSIVE CORRELATION MATRIX

cat("Creating comprehensive correlation matrix with improved data handling...\n")

# Load required libraries
if (!require(corrplot)) install.packages("corrplot")
if (!require(Hmisc)) install.packages("Hmisc")
if (!require(dplyr)) install.packages("dplyr")
if (!require(ggplot2)) install.packages("ggplot2")
if (!require(reshape2)) install.packages("reshape2")

library(corrplot)
library(Hmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

# Define numeric variables with better categorization
production_vars <- c(
  "tc_per_ha_estimated", "tc_estimated", "tc_actual", "tc_actual_per_week",
  "tc_per_ha_actual", "tc_per_ha_per_week", "tc_52_weeks", "tc_per_ha_52_weeks",
  "tons_per_harvest", "tons_per_week_actual", "tons_per_ha", "tons_per_ha_per_week",
  "tons_52_weeks", "tons_per_ha_52_weeks", "potential_yield", "potential_tc"
)

quality_vars <- c(
  "brix_percent", "pol_juice_percent", "purity_percent", "fiber_percent",
  "pol_cane_percent", "percent_cane_percent", "glucose_cane_percent",
  "hugot_sugar", "purity_tc_percent", "fiber_content_percent",
  "juice_tons", "tmss", "tpj", "tpc", "ts", "tsr"
)

temporal_vars <- c(
```
