## III.1. Sugarcane crop calendar and phenology analysis

```{r}
# ===============================================================================
# SUGARCANE CROP CALENDAR AND PHENOLOGY ANALYSIS
# Time series analysis of crop stages and phenological patterns
# ===============================================================================

# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Check for additional packages
if (!require(RColorBrewer, quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("RColorBrewer", quiet = TRUE)
  library(RColorBrewer)
}

if (!require(gridExtra, quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("gridExtra", quiet = TRUE)
  library(gridExtra)
}

# Try to load scales for better formatting
scales_available <- require(scales, quietly = TRUE)

cat("=== SUGARCANE CROP CALENDAR AND PHENOLOGY ANALYSIS ===\n\n")

# ===============================================================================
# DATA PREPARATION FOR PHENOLOGY ANALYSIS
# ===============================================================================

# Function to create crop calendar data
create_crop_calendar <- function(data) {
  
  # Filter valid data
  valid_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(planting_date_clean) & !is.na(harvest_date_clean)) %>%
    filter(growing_days > 0 & growing_days < 730) %>%  # Reasonable growing periods
    mutate(
      planting_doy = yday(planting_date_clean),  # Day of year
      harvest_doy = yday(harvest_date_clean),
      planting_month_num = month(planting_date_clean),
      harvest_month_num = month(harvest_date_clean),
      planting_year = year(planting_date_clean),
      harvest_year = year(harvest_date_clean)
    )
  
  return(valid_data)
}

# Function to estimate crop phenology stages
estimate_phenology_stages <- function(planting_date, harvest_date, growing_days) {
  
  # Sugarcane typical growth stages (approximate percentages of total growing period)
  stages <- list(
    germination = 0.08,      # ~8% - Germination and establishment (0-1.5 months)
    tillering = 0.25,        # ~25% - Tillering phase (1.5-4 months)  
    grand_growth = 0.50,     # ~50% - Grand growth phase (4-8 months)
    maturation = 0.85,       # ~85% - Maturation phase (8-12+ months)
    harvest = 1.0            # 100% - Harvest ready
  )
  
  stage_dates <- data.frame(
    stage = names(stages),
    days_from_planting = round(unlist(stages) * growing_days),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      stage_date = planting_date + days(days_from_planting),
      stage_doy = yday(stage_date),
      stage_month = month(stage_date),
      stage_week = week(stage_date)
    )
  
  return(stage_dates)
}

# ===============================================================================
# MAIN ANALYSIS
# ===============================================================================

cat("1. PREPARING CROP CALENDAR DATA...\n")

# Prepare the main dataset
crop_calendar_data <- create_crop_calendar(analysis_data)

cat("Valid records for phenology analysis:", nrow(crop_calendar_data), "\n")

if (nrow(crop_calendar_data) == 0) {
  stop("No valid data found for crop calendar analysis. Check your date fields.")
}

# ===============================================================================
# PHENOLOGY STAGE ANALYSIS
# ===============================================================================

cat("\n2. ANALYZING CROP PHENOLOGY STAGES...\n")

# Calculate phenology stages for each record
phenology_data <- crop_calendar_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  do({
    stages_df <- estimate_phenology_stages(.$planting_date_clean, 
                                         .$harvest_date_clean, 
                                         .$growing_days)
    stages_df$record_id <- .$parcel_id
    stages_df$campaign <- .$campaign
    stages_df$crop_type <- .$crop_type
    stages_df$variety <- if("variety" %in% names(.)) .$variety else "Unknown"
    stages_df
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate average timing for each phenology stage
phenology_summary <- phenology_data %>%
  group_by(stage) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_days_from_planting = round(mean(days_from_planting, na.rm = TRUE)),
    avg_doy = round(mean(stage_doy, na.rm = TRUE)),
    avg_month = round(mean(stage_month, na.rm = TRUE)),
    median_doy = round(median(stage_doy, na.rm = TRUE)),
    min_doy = min(stage_doy, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_doy = max(stage_doy, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_month_name = month.name[avg_month],
    stage_label = case_when(
      stage == "germination" ~ "Germination & Establishment",
      stage == "tillering" ~ "Tillering Phase",
      stage == "grand_growth" ~ "Grand Growth Phase", 
      stage == "maturation" ~ "Maturation Phase",
      stage == "harvest" ~ "Harvest Ready",
      TRUE ~ stage
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(avg_days_from_planting)

print(phenology_summary)

# ===============================================================================
# MONTHLY ACTIVITY PATTERNS
# ===============================================================================

cat("\n3. ANALYZING MONTHLY ACTIVITY PATTERNS...\n")

# Monthly planting and harvest patterns
monthly_patterns <- crop_calendar_data %>%
  select(planting_month_num, harvest_month_num) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "activity", values_to = "month") %>%
  mutate(
    activity = case_when(
      activity == "planting_month_num" ~ "Planting",
      activity == "harvest_month_num" ~ "Harvest"
    ),
    month_name = month.name[month]
  ) %>%
  count(activity, month_name, month) %>%
  group_by(activity) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month.name)
  ) %>%
  arrange(activity, month)

# Peak months for each activity
peak_months <- monthly_patterns %>%
  group_by(activity) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 3) %>%
  summarise(
    peak_months = paste(month_name, collapse = ", "),
    peak_percentages = paste(paste0(percentage, "%"), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

cat("Peak activity months:\n")
print(peak_months)

# ===============================================================================
# CROP TYPE DIFFERENCES
# ===============================================================================

cat("\n4. ANALYZING CROP TYPE DIFFERENCES...\n")

crop_type_patterns <- crop_calendar_data %>%
  filter(crop_type %in% c("Plant Cane", "Ratoon")) %>%
  group_by(crop_type) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_growing_days = round(mean(growing_days, na.rm = TRUE)),
    avg_growing_months = round(mean(growing_days / 30.44, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    
    # Most common planting months
    most_common_planting_month = names(sort(table(planting_month_num), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    
    # Most common harvest months  
    most_common_harvest_month = names(sort(table(harvest_month_num), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    
    n_records = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    planting_month_name = month.name[as.numeric(most_common_planting_month)],
    harvest_month_name = month.name[as.numeric(most_common_harvest_month)]
  )

print(crop_type_patterns)

# ===============================================================================
# PLOTTING SECTION
# ===============================================================================

cat("\n5. CREATING CROP CALENDAR VISUALIZATIONS...\n")

# Define plotting parameters
plot_width <- 14
plot_height <- 10
plot_dpi <- 300

# Common theme for crop calendar plots
calendar_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 20)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )

# Color palettes
stage_colors <- c(
  "Germination & Establishment" = "#8FBC8F",
  "Tillering Phase" = "#32CD32", 
  "Grand Growth Phase" = "#228B22",
  "Maturation Phase" = "#DAA520",
  "Harvest Ready" = "#CD853F"
)

activity_colors <- c("Planting" = "#228B22", "Harvest" = "#DAA520")
crop_type_colors <- c("Plant Cane" = "#2E8B57", "Ratoon" = "#CD853F")

# ===============================================================================
# PLOT 1: CROP PHENOLOGY CALENDAR (CIRCULAR)
# ===============================================================================

cat("Creating Plot 1: Circular Crop Calendar...\n")

# Prepare data for circular plot
circular_data <- phenology_summary %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert day of year to angle (360 degrees / 365 days)
    angle = (avg_doy / 365) * 360,
    # Position stages at different radii
    radius = case_when(
      stage == "germination" ~ 1,
      stage == "tillering" ~ 2, 
      stage == "grand_growth" ~ 3,
      stage == "maturation" ~ 4,
      stage == "harvest" ~ 5
    )
  )

# Create month positions for circular plot
month_positions <- data.frame(
  month = 1:12,
  month_name = month.abb,
  angle = (((1:12 - 1) * 30) + 15),  # Middle of each month
  radius = 6
)

p1 <- ggplot() +
  # Add month labels around the outside
  geom_text(data = month_positions, aes(x = angle, y = radius, label = month_name),
            size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Add phenology stages
  geom_point(data = circular_data, aes(x = angle, y = radius, color = stage_label),
             size = 6, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = circular_data, aes(x = angle, y = radius - 0.3, label = stage_label),
            size = 3, angle = 45, hjust = 0) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = stage_colors, name = "Growth Stage") +
  coord_polar(theta = "x", start = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 360), breaks = seq(0, 330, 30)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) +
  labs(
    title = "Sugarcane Phenology Calendar",
    subtitle = "Circular calendar showing average timing of crop growth stages throughout the year"
  ) +
  calendar_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

ggsave("Crop_Calendar_01_Circular_Phenology.png", p1, width = 12, height = 12, dpi = plot_dpi)

# ===============================================================================
# PLOT 2: MONTHLY ACTIVITY PATTERNS
# ===============================================================================

cat("Creating Plot 2: Monthly Activity Patterns...\n")

p2 <- ggplot(monthly_patterns, aes(x = month_name, y = percentage, fill = activity)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(percentage, "%")), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = activity_colors, name = "Activity") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), 
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal Distribution of Planting and Harvest Activities",
    subtitle = "Percentage of activities by month showing peak seasons for crop management",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Percentage of Activities"
  ) +
  calendar_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave("Crop_Calendar_02_Monthly_Patterns.png", p2, width = plot_width, height = 8, dpi = plot_dpi)

# ===============================================================================
# PLOT 3: PHENOLOGY TIMELINE BY CROP TYPE
# ===============================================================================

cat("Creating Plot 3: Phenology Timeline by Crop Type...\n")

# Prepare timeline data
timeline_data <- phenology_data %>%
  filter(crop_type %in% c("Plant Cane", "Ratoon")) %>%
  mutate(
    stage_order = case_when(
      stage == "germination" ~ 1,
      stage == "tillering" ~ 2,
      stage == "grand_growth" ~ 3,
      stage == "maturation" ~ 4,
      stage == "harvest" ~ 5
    ),
    stage_label = case_when(
      stage == "germination" ~ "Germination",
      stage == "tillering" ~ "Tillering",
      stage == "grand_growth" ~ "Grand Growth",
      stage == "maturation" ~ "Maturation",
      stage == "harvest" ~ "Harvest",
      TRUE ~ stage
    )
  )

# Calculate average timeline by crop type
timeline_summary <- timeline_data %>%
  group_by(crop_type, stage, stage_label, stage_order) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_days = round(mean(days_from_planting, na.rm = TRUE)),
    avg_months = round(avg_days / 30.44, 1),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(crop_type, stage_order)

p3 <- ggplot(timeline_summary, aes(x = avg_months, y = reorder(stage_label, -stage_order), 
                                   fill = crop_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(avg_months, "m")), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = crop_type_colors, name = "Crop Type") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Crop Phenology Timeline: Plant Cane vs Ratoon",
    subtitle = "Average timing of growth stages from planting (months)",
    x = "Months from Planting",
    y = "Growth Stage"
  ) +
  calendar_theme

ggsave("Crop_Calendar_03_Phenology_Timeline.png", p3, width = plot_width, height = 8, dpi = plot_dpi)

# ===============================================================================
# PLOT 4: GROWING PERIOD DISTRIBUTION BY MONTH
# ===============================================================================

cat("Creating Plot 4: Growing Period by Planting Month...\n")

growing_by_month <- crop_calendar_data %>%
  mutate(
    planting_month_name = month.name[planting_month_num],

p4 <- ggplot(growing_by_month, aes(x = planting_month_name, y = growing_days / 30.44)) +

    x = "Planting Month",
    y = "Growing Period (months)"
  ) +
  calendar_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave("Crop_Calendar_04_Growing_Period_by_Month.png", p4, width = plot_width, height = 8, dpi = plot_dpi)

# ===============================================================================
# PLOT 5: COMPREHENSIVE CROP CALENDAR HEATMAP
# ===============================================================================

cat("Creating Plot 5: Crop Calendar Heatmap...\n")

# Create a heatmap showing activity intensity throughout the year
heatmap_data <- crop_calendar_data %>%
  select(planting_date_clean, harvest_date_clean) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "activity", values_to = "date") %>%
  mutate(
    activity = case_when(
      activity == "planting_date_clean" ~ "Planting",
      activity == "harvest_date_clean" ~ "Harvest"
    ),
    month = month(date),
    week = week(date),
    year = year(date)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(date)) %>%
  count(activity, month, week) %>%
  complete(activity, month = 1:12, week = 1:53, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = month.name[month],
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month.name)
  )

p5 <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = week, y = month_name, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#228B22", name = "Activity\nCount") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 52, 4), labels = paste0("Week ", seq(1, 52, 4))) +
  facet_wrap(~activity, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Crop Calendar Activity Heatmap",
    subtitle = "Intensity of planting and harvest activities throughout the year",
    x = "Week of Year",
    y = "Month"
  ) +
  calendar_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )

ggsave("Crop_Calendar_05_Activity_Heatmap.png", p5, width = plot_width, height = 10, dpi = plot_dpi)

# ===============================================================================
# PLOT 6: INTEGRATED CROP CALENDAR DASHBOARD
# ===============================================================================

# Create mini versions for dashboard

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8)
  )

# Mini plot 1: Monthly distribution pie chart

  group_by(month_name) %>%

# Mini plot 2: Crop type comparison
dash_p2 <- ggplot(crop_type_patterns, aes(x = crop_type, y = avg_growing_months, fill = crop_type)) +

# Mini plot 3: Phenology stages
stage_summary_simple <- phenology_summary %>%

dash_p3 <- ggplot(stage_summary_simple, aes(x = avg_months, y = reorder(stage_label, avg_months))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4472C4", alpha = 0.7, width = 0.6) +

# Mini plot 4: Key statistics

  "Crop Calendar Summary:\n\n",

)

dash_p4 <- ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 0.05, y = 0.5, label = key_stats, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, 
           size = 3, lineheight = 1.2) +

  labs(title = "Key Statistics") +
  dash_theme +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank())

# Combine dashboard

                         ncol = 2, nrow = 2,
                         top = textGrob("Sugarcane Crop Calendar Dashboard", 
                                       gp = gpar(fontsize = 16, fontface = "bold")))

ggsave("Crop_Calendar_06_Dashboard.png", dashboard, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = plot_dpi)

# ===============================================================================
# SUMMARY REPORT
# ===============================================================================

cat("\n6. CROP CALENDAR ANALYSIS SUMMARY\n")
cat("==================================\n")

cat("PHENOLOGY STAGES (Average Timing):\n")
for(i in 1:nrow(phenology_summary)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-25s: %3d days (%4.1f months) - %s\n", 
              phenology_summary$stage_label[i],
              phenology_summary$avg_days_from_planting[i],
              phenology_summary$avg_days_from_planting[i] / 30.44,
              phenology_summary$avg_month_name[i]))
}

cat("\nPEAK ACTIVITY PERIODS:\n")
cat("Planting:", peak_months$peak_months[peak_months$activity == "Planting"], "\n")
cat("Harvest: ", peak_months$peak_months[peak_months$activity == "Harvest"], "\n")

cat("\nCROP TYPE DIFFERENCES:\n")
for(i in 1:nrow(crop_type_patterns)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-12s: %4.1f months growing period, plants in %s, harvests in %s\n",
              crop_type_patterns$crop_type[i],
              crop_type_patterns$avg_growing_months[i],
              crop_type_patterns$planting_month_name[i],
              crop_type_patterns$harvest_month_name[i]))
}
```

## III.2. Varieties analysis

```{r}
# Sugarcane Variety Analysis Script
# Comprehensive analysis with  visualizations

# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(gridExtra)

# Check if data exists
if (!exists("data")) {
  stop("Error: 'data' object not found. Please load your sugarcane dataset first.")
}

# Data preparation
cat("=== PREPARING DATA FOR VARIETY ANALYSIS ===\n")

# Debug: Check original data structure
cat("Original data structure:\n")
cat("Columns:", paste(names(data), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Total rows:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Campaign column type:", class(data$campaign), "\n")
cat("Variety column type:", class(data$variety), "\n")

# Show sample of original campaigns
if("campaign" %in% names(data)) {
  cat("Original campaign values (first 10):\n")
  print(head(unique(data$campaign), 10))
} else {
  cat("Warning: 'campaign' column not found!\n")
}

# Clean and prepare the data with better error handling
analysis_data <- data %>%
  # Convert to character first to avoid factor issues
  mutate(
    campaign = as.character(campaign),
    variety = as.character(variety),
    block = if("block" %in% names(.)) as.character(block) else "Unknown"
  ) %>%
  # Filter step by step with diagnostics
  filter(!is.na(campaign), !is.na(variety)) %>%
  filter(if("surface_area_ha" %in% names(.)) !is.na(surface_area_ha) else TRUE) %>%
  filter(if("surface_area_ha" %in% names(.)) surface_area_ha > 0 else TRUE)

# Show converted campaigns
cat("Converted campaign values (first 10):\n")
print(head(unique(analysis_data$campaign), 10))

# Data quality check
cat("Data quality check:\n")
cat("Total rows:", nrow(analysis_data), "\n")
cat("Rows with valid variety:", sum(!is.na(analysis_data$variety)), "\n")
cat("Rows with valid campaign:", sum(!is.na(analysis_data$campaign)), "\n")
if("surface_area_ha" %in% names(analysis_data)) {
  cat("Rows with valid surface:", sum(!is.na(analysis_data$surface_area_ha)), "\n")
  analysis_data <- analysis_data %>% filter(surface_area_ha < 1000)
  cat("Rows after filtering:", nrow(analysis_data), "\n")
}

# Handle campaign ordering more robustly
if(nrow(analysis_data) > 0) {
  # Try to extract year from campaign string
  analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
    mutate(
      campaign_start_year = case_when(
        # Format: "YY-YY" (e.g., "21-22")
        nchar(campaign) == 5 & grepl("^[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$", campaign) ~ 
          as.numeric(paste0("20", substr(campaign, 1, 2))),
        # Format: "YYYY-YY" (e.g., "2021-22")
        nchar(campaign) == 7 & grepl("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}$", campaign) ~ 
          as.numeric(substr(campaign, 1, 4)),
        # Format: "YYYY" (e.g., "2021")
        nchar(campaign) == 4 & grepl("^[0-9]{4}$", campaign) ~ 
          as.numeric(campaign),
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      )
    )
  
  # Show campaign range
  cat("Campaign range:", min(analysis_data$campaign_start_year, na.rm = TRUE), 
      max(analysis_data$campaign_start_year, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  
  # Get ordered campaigns
  campaign_summary <- analysis_data %>%
    group_by(campaign) %>%
    summarise(
      first = min(campaign_start_year, na.rm = TRUE),
      count = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(first, campaign)
  
  campaign_order <- campaign_summary$campaign
  analysis_data$campaign <- factor(analysis_data$campaign, levels = campaign_order)
} else {
  stop("No data remaining after filtering. Please check your data structure and column names.")
}

cat("Data prepared successfully!\n")
cat("Campaigns found:", length(unique(analysis_data$campaign)), "\n")
cat("Varieties found:", length(unique(analysis_data$variety)), "\n")
cat("Blocks found:", length(unique(analysis_data$block)), "\n")
cat("Total surface area:", round(sum(analysis_data$surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "ha\n\n")

# Define consistent theme
theme_custom <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # Text elements
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    
    # Legend
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
    legend.margin = margin(l = 20),
    
    # Grid and background
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    
    # Facets (for multi-panel plots)
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray80")
  )
}

# Get top varieties by total surface area (use ALL varieties, but group smaller ones)
top_varieties_full <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(total_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_surface))

# Take top 12 varieties, group the rest as "Others"
top_varieties <- head(top_varieties_full, 12)$variety

# Create enhanced color palette
colors_main <- c(
  viridis(8, option = "viridis"),
  brewer.pal(4, "Set2")
)
colors_final <- c(colors_main, "gray60")  # Gray for "Others"
names(colors_final) <- c(top_varieties, "Others")[1:13]

# ===== CAMPAIGN-BASED ANALYSIS =====

cat("=== CAMPAIGN-BASED VARIETY ANALYSIS ===\n")

# Prepare data with proper ordering (most important varieties first)
prepare_ordered_data <- function(data_input, group_var, value_var) {
  # Get variety order by total values (descending)
  variety_order <- data_input %>%
    group_by(variety) %>%
    summarise(total_val = sum(!!sym(value_var)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(total_val)) %>%
    pull(variety)
  
  # Create variety groups and reorder - CORRECT ORDER for stacking
  result <- data_input %>%
    mutate(
      variety_group = ifelse(variety %in% top_varieties, variety, "Others"),
      # Order varieties from bottom to top (smallest to largest at bottom)
      variety_group = factor(variety_group, levels = c("Others", top_varieties))
    ) %>%
    group_by(!!sym(group_var), variety_group) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(!!sym(value_var)), .groups = "drop")
  
  return(result)
}

# 1. Surface area by variety per campaign (ALL CAMPAIGNS)
surface_by_variety_campaign <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(campaign, variety) %>%
  summarise(
    total_surface_ha = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    parcels_count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

surface_data_ordered <- prepare_ordered_data(surface_by_variety_campaign, "campaign", "total_surface_ha")

# PLOT 1: Enhanced stacked bar chart - Surface area by variety per campaign
p1 <- ggplot(surface_data_ordered, aes(x = campaign, y = value, fill = variety_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_final, name = "Variety") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Surface Area Evolution by Variety Across All Campaigns",
    subtitle = "Hectares planted per variety (most important varieties at top)",
    x = "Campaign",
    y = "Surface Area (hectares)"
  ) +
  theme_custom()

print(p1)

# 2. Number of parcels by variety per campaign (ALL CAMPAIGNS)
parcel_count_by_variety <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(campaign, variety) %>%
  summarise(parcel_count = n(), .groups = "drop")

parcel_data_ordered <- prepare_ordered_data(parcel_count_by_variety, "campaign", "parcel_count")

# PLOT 2: Enhanced stacked bar chart - Parcel count
p2 <- ggplot(parcel_data_ordered, aes(x = campaign, y = value, fill = variety_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_final, name = "Variety") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Parcel Count Evolution by Variety Across All Campaigns",
    subtitle = "Number of parcels planted per variety (most important varieties at top)",
    x = "Campaign",
    y = "Number of Parcels"
  ) +
  theme_custom()

print(p2)

# ===== BLOCK-BASED ANALYSIS (ALL BLOCKS) =====

cat("\n=== BLOCK-BASED VARIETY ANALYSIS FOR ALL BLOCKS ===\n")

# Get all blocks with meaningful data
all_blocks_summary <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(block) %>%
  summarise(
    campaigns = n_distinct(campaign),
    varieties = n_distinct(variety),
    total_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_parcels = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(campaigns >= 2, total_surface >= 5) %>%  # Blocks with at least 2 campaigns and 5 ha
  arrange(desc(total_surface))

selected_blocks_all <- all_blocks_summary$block

cat("Analyzing all relevant blocks:", length(selected_blocks_all), "\n")

# Block analysis data for ALL qualifying blocks
block_analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(block %in% selected_blocks_all)

# Prepare block data with proper ordering
prepare_block_data <- function(data_input, value_var) {
  result <- data_input %>%
    mutate(
      variety_group = ifelse(variety %in% top_varieties, variety, "Others"),
      # Order varieties from bottom to top for correct stacking
      variety_group = factor(variety_group, levels = c("Others", top_varieties))
    ) %>%
    group_by(block, campaign, variety_group) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(!!sym(value_var)), .groups = "drop")
  
  return(result)
}

# PLOT 3: Enhanced parcels by block (ALL BLOCKS with facet_wrap)
variety_count_by_block <- block_analysis_data %>%
  group_by(block, campaign, variety) %>%
  summarise(parcels = n(), .groups = "drop")

parcel_block_ordered <- prepare_block_data(variety_count_by_block, "parcels")

p3 <- ggplot(parcel_block_ordered, aes(x = campaign, y = value, fill = variety_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_final, name = "Variety") +
  facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Parcel Count Evolution by Variety for All Blocks",
    subtitle = "Number of parcels per variety across campaigns",
    x = "Campaign",
    y = "Number of Parcels"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

print(p3)

# PLOT 4: Enhanced surface area by block (ALL BLOCKS)
surface_by_block <- block_analysis_data %>%
  group_by(block, campaign, variety) %>%
  summarise(total_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

surface_block_ordered <- prepare_block_data(surface_by_block, "total_surface")

p4 <- ggplot(surface_block_ordered, aes(x = campaign, y = value, fill = variety_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_final, name = "Variety") +
  facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Surface Area Evolution by Variety for All Blocks",
    subtitle = "Surface area (hectares) per variety across campaigns",
    x = "Campaign",
    y = "Surface Area (hectares)"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

print(p4)

# ===== VARIETY DIVERSITY ANALYSIS =====

cat("\n=== VARIETY DIVERSITY ANALYSIS ===\n")

# Calculate diversity metrics for ALL campaigns
diversity_by_campaign <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(campaign) %>%
  summarise(
    unique_varieties = n_distinct(variety),
    total_parcels = n(),
    total_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    varieties_per_100ha = unique_varieties / (total_surface / 100),
    parcels_per_variety = total_parcels / unique_varieties
  )

# PLOT 5: Enhanced variety diversity trends
p5 <- ggplot(diversity_by_campaign, aes(x = campaign)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = unique_varieties), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8, width = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = varieties_per_100ha * 3, group = 1), 
            color = "red", size = 1.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(y = varieties_per_100ha * 3), 
             color = "red", size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of Unique Varieties",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 3, name = "Varieties per 100 hectares", labels = comma_format()),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Variety Diversity Evolution Across All Campaigns",
    subtitle = "Blue bars: Total unique varieties | Red line: Variety density per 100 hectares",
    x = "Campaign"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = "steelblue"),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "red"),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "red"),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(color = "steelblue")
  )

print(p5)

# ===== SUMMARY STATISTICS =====

cat("\n=== ENHANCED SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")

# Overall variety statistics
cat("OVERALL VARIETY STATISTICS:\n")
cat("Total unique varieties:", n_distinct(analysis_data$variety), "\n")
cat("Total campaigns analyzed:", n_distinct(analysis_data$campaign), "\n")
cat("Total blocks analyzed:", n_distinct(analysis_data$block), "\n")
cat("Total surface area:", round(sum(analysis_data$surface_area_ha), 2), "hectares\n")
cat("Average surface per parcel:", round(mean(analysis_data$surface_area_ha), 2), "hectares\n\n")

# Enhanced top varieties summary
top_varieties_summary <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(
    total_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_parcels = n(),
    campaigns_present = n_distinct(campaign),
    blocks_present = n_distinct(block),
    avg_parcel_size = mean(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    surface_percentage = total_surface / sum(analysis_data$surface_area_ha) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_surface)) %>%
  head(15)

cat("TOP 15 VARIETIES BY TOTAL SURFACE AREA:\n")
print(top_varieties_summary)

# Block coverage summary
block_summary_final <- all_blocks_summary %>%
  summarise(
    total_blocks = n(),
    avg_campaigns_per_block = mean(campaigns),
    avg_varieties_per_block = mean(varieties),
    avg_surface_per_block = mean(total_surface),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nBLOCK COVERAGE SUMMARY:\n")
print(block_summary_final)
```

```{r}
      variety_group = ifelse(variety %in% top_varieties, variety, "Others"),
      # Order varieties from bottom to top (smallest to largest at bottom)
      variety_group = factor(variety_group, levels = c("Others", top_varieties))
    ) %>%
    group_by(!!sym(group_var), variety_group) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(!!sym(value_var)), .groups = "drop")
  
  return(result)
}

# Prepare block data with proper ordering
prepare_block_data <- function(data_input, value_var) {
  result <- data_input %>%
    mutate(
      variety_group = ifelse(variety %in% top_varieties, variety, "Others"),
      # Order varieties from bottom to top for correct stacking
      variety_group = factor(variety_group, levels = c("Others", top_varieties))
    ) %>%
    group_by(block, campaign, variety_group) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(!!sym(value_var)), .groups = "drop")
  
  return(result)
}

# PLOT 8: Variety lifecycle analysis - First vs Last appearance
variety_lifecycle <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(
    first_campaign = min(as.numeric(campaign), na.rm = TRUE),
    last_campaign = max(as.numeric(campaign), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_campaigns = n_distinct(campaign),
    total_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_surface_per_campaign = total_surface / total_campaigns,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    variety_lifespan = last_campaign - first_campaign + 1,
    variety_status = case_when(
      last_campaign == max(last_campaign) & total_campaigns >= 3 ~ "Active (Established)",
      last_campaign == max(last_campaign) & total_campaigns < 3 ~ "Active (Recent)",
      last_campaign < max(last_campaign) & total_campaigns >= 3 ~ "Discontinued",
      TRUE ~ "Experimental"
    )
  )

p8 <- ggplot(variety_lifecycle, aes(x = first_campaign, y = avg_surface_per_campaign,

  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Active (Established)" = "darkgreen", 
                               "Active (Recent)" = "lightgreen",
                               "Discontinued" = "red",
                               "Experimental" = "orange")) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), name = "Total Campaigns") +
  labs(
    title = "Variety Lifecycle Analysis",
    subtitle = "When varieties were introduced and their average performance",
    x = "First Campaign (Index)",
    y = "Average Surface Area per Campaign (ha)",
    color = "Variety Status"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5)))

print(p8)

# PLOT 9: Variety stability analysis - Coefficient of variation
variety_stability <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety, campaign) %>%
  summarise(campaign_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%  # Only varieties with at least 3 campaigns
  summarise(
    campaigns_count = n(),
    mean_surface = mean(campaign_surface),
    sd_surface = sd(campaign_surface),
    total_surface = sum(campaign_surface),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cv = sd_surface / mean_surface,
    stability_category = case_when(
      cv <= 0.3 ~ "Very Stable",
      cv <= 0.5 ~ "Stable", 
      cv <= 0.8 ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE ~ "Variable"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cv), !is.infinite(cv))

p9 <- ggplot(variety_stability, aes(x = mean_surface, y = cv, color = stability_category, size = total_surface)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Very Stable" = "darkgreen", "Stable" = "green", 
                               "Moderate" = "orange", "Variable" = "red")) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma_format()) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), name = "Total Surface (ha)") +
  labs(
    title = "Variety Stability Analysis",
    subtitle = "Surface area consistency across campaigns (3+ campaigns only)",
    x = "Average Surface Area per Campaign (ha, log scale)",
    y = "Coefficient of Variation (CV)",
    color = "Stability Category"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.8), linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5)

print(p9)

# PLOT 10: Variety adoption trends - Growth rate analysis
variety_trends <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety, campaign) %>%
  summarise(campaign_surface = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%  # At least 5 campaigns for trend analysis
  arrange(campaign) %>%
  mutate(
    campaign_num = row_number(),
    surface_change = campaign_surface - lag(campaign_surface),
    pct_change = (campaign_surface - lag(campaign_surface)) / lag(campaign_surface) * 100
  ) %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(
    campaigns_count = n(),
    first_surface = first(campaign_surface),
    last_surface = last(campaign_surface),
    total_surface = sum(campaign_surface),
    avg_change = mean(surface_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    trend_slope = if(campaigns_count > 1) lm(campaign_surface ~ campaign_num)$coefficients[2] else 0,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    growth_rate = (last_surface - first_surface) / first_surface * 100,
    trend_category = case_when(
      trend_slope > 50 ~ "Strong Growth",
      trend_slope > 10 ~ "Growing",
      trend_slope > -10 ~ "Stable",
      trend_slope > -50 ~ "Declining",
      TRUE ~ "Strong Decline"
    )
  )

p10 <- ggplot(variety_trends, aes(x = first_surface, y = last_surface, color = trend_category, size = total_surface)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Strong Growth" = "darkgreen", "Growing" = "lightgreen",
                               "Stable" = "blue", "Declining" = "orange", 
                               "Strong Decline" = "red")) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma_format()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = comma_format()) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), name = "Total Surface (ha)") +
  labs(
    title = "Variety Adoption Trends",
    subtitle = "First vs Last campaign surface area (5+ campaigns only)",
    x = "First Campaign Surface Area (ha, log scale)",
    y = "Last Campaign Surface Area (ha, log scale)",
    color = "Trend Category"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5))) +
  annotate("text", x = max(variety_trends$first_surface) * 0.1, 
           y = max(variety_trends$last_surface) * 0.8,
           label = "Above line = Growth\nBelow line = Decline", 
           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "gray50")

print(p10)

# Summary insights
cat("\n=== EXPLORATORY ANALYSIS INSIGHTS ===\n")

cat("VARIETY CONCENTRATION (", as.character(last_campaign), "):\n")
top_varieties_80 <- last_campaign_data %>% filter(cumulative_percent <= 80) %>% nrow()
cat("- Number of varieties covering 80% of surface:", top_varieties_80, "\n")
cat("- Top 3 varieties cover:", round(last_campaign_data$cumulative_percent[3], 1), "% of surface\n")

cat("\nVARIETY LIFECYCLE STATUS:\n")
lifecycle_summary <- variety_lifecycle %>% count(variety_status) %>% arrange(desc(n))
print(lifecycle_summary)

cat("\nVARIETY STABILITY SUMMARY:\n")
stability_summary <- variety_stability %>% count(stability_category) %>% arrange(desc(n))
print(stability_summary)

cat("\nVARIETY TREND SUMMARY:\n")
trend_summary <- variety_trends %>% count(trend_category) %>% arrange(desc(n))
print(trend_summary)

cat("\n=== COMPLETE ANALYSIS FINISHED ===\n")
```

## III.3. Harvest and Irrigation Analysis

```{r}
# Harvest and Irrigation Analysis
# Deep analysis with professional visualizations

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)

# Check if data exists
if (!exists("data")) {
  stop("Error: Please load your sugarcane dataset first.")
}

cat("=== HARVEST & IRRIGATION ANALYSIS ===\n")

# ===== DATA PREPARATION =====
analysis_data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean harvest and irrigation data
    harvest = ifelse(is.na(harvest) | harvest == "", "Unknown", as.character(harvest)),
    irrigation_type = ifelse(is.na(irrigation_type) | irrigation_type == "", "Unknown", as.character(irrigation_type)),
    # Handle surface area
    surface_area_ha = ifelse(is.na(surface_area_ha), 1, surface_area_ha)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(campaign), !is.na(variety), surface_area_ha > 0)

# Fix encoding issues after initial data preparation
analysis_data$harvest <- iconv(analysis_data$harvest, from = "latin1", to = "UTF-8")
analysis_data$harvest <- ifelse(grepl("canique", analysis_data$harvest, ignore.case = TRUE), "Mechanical", analysis_data$harvest)
analysis_data$harvest <- ifelse(grepl("Manuelle", analysis_data$harvest, ignore.case = TRUE), "Manual", analysis_data$harvest)

cat("Data prepared:", nrow(analysis_data), "records\n")
cat("Harvest methods:", paste(unique(analysis_data$harvest), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Irrigation types:", paste(unique(analysis_data$irrigation_type), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# Define consistent theme
theme_custom <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # Text elements
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    
    # Legend
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
    legend.margin = margin(l = 20),
    
    # Grid and background
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    
    # Facets (for multi-panel plots)
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray80")
  )
}

# Color palettes
harvest_colors <- c("Manual" = "#2E8B57", "Mechanical" = "#FF6B35", "Unknown" = "#95A5A6")
irrigation_colors <- c("GRV" = "#3498DB", "GAG" = "#E74C3C", "Unknown" = "#95A5A6")

# ===== HARVEST METHOD ANALYSIS =====

# Summary by harvest method
harvest_summary <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(harvest) %>%
  summarise(
    total_hectares = sum(surface_area_ha),
    total_parcels = n(),
    percentage = round(sum(surface_area_ha) / sum(analysis_data$surface_area_ha) * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_hectares))

cat("HARVEST METHODS:\n")
print(harvest_summary)

# Plot 1: Enhanced Harvest methods distribution with detailed labels
p1 <- ggplot(harvest_summary, aes(x = reorder(harvest, total_hectares), y = total_hectares)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = harvest), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(comma(total_hectares), " ha\n(", percentage, "%)")), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = harvest_colors, name = "Harvest Method") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Harvest Methods Distribution by Surface Area",
    subtitle = "Total cultivated area analyzed across all campaigns",
    x = "Harvest Method",
    y = "Surface Area (hectares)"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  guides(fill = "none")  # Remove legend since colors are self-explanatory

print(p1)

# Plot 2: Enhanced Harvest methods evolution with percentage stacking
harvest_by_campaign_pct <- harvest_by_campaign %>%
  group_by(campaign) %>%
```

### III.2.1. Block-Variety Affinity Analysis

```{r}
# Block-Variety Affinity Analysis
# Analyzing variety preferences and dominance patterns by block over time

if (!require(ggplot2)) library(ggplot2)
if (!require(dplyr)) library(dplyr)
if (!require(tidyr)) library(tidyr)
if (!require(RColorBrewer)) library(RColorBrewer)
if (!require(viridis)) library(viridis)
if (!require(scales)) library(scales)
if (!require(gridExtra)) library(gridExtra)

cat("=== BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY ANALYSIS ===\n")

# Ensure we have the necessary data (from previous analysis)
if (!exists("analysis_data")) {
  stop("Error: 'analysis_data' not found. Please run the main variety analysis script first.")
}

# Convert variety names to uppercase for consistency
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(variety = toupper(variety))

cat("Variety names converted to uppercase\n")

# Use the same theme from previous analysis
if (!exists("theme_custom")) {
  theme_custom <- function() {
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 8)),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray80")
    )
  }
}

# ===== BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY CALCULATIONS =====

# Calculate variety dominance by block across all campaigns
block_variety_affinity <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(block, variety) %>%
  summarise(
    total_surface_ha = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_parcels = n(),
    campaigns_present = n_distinct(campaign),
    avg_parcel_size = mean(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Calculate percentage within each block
  group_by(block) %>%
  mutate(
    block_total_surface = sum(total_surface_ha),
    variety_percentage = (total_surface_ha / block_total_surface) * 100,
    variety_rank = rank(desc(total_surface_ha), ties.method = "first")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Filter for meaningful blocks (at least 10 ha total)
  filter(block_total_surface >= 10)

# Identify blocks with strong variety preferences (where top variety > 40% or top 3 varieties > 80%)
strong_affinity_blocks <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  group_by(block) %>%
  summarise(
    top1_percentage = max(variety_percentage),
    top3_percentage = sum(head(sort(variety_percentage, decreasing = TRUE), 3)),
    dominant_variety = variety[which.max(variety_percentage)],
    total_varieties = n_distinct(variety),
    total_surface = first(block_total_surface),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(top1_percentage > 25 | top3_percentage > 70) %>%  # Blocks with clear preferences
  arrange(desc(top1_percentage))

cat("BLOCKS WITH STRONG VARIETY AFFINITIES:\n")
print(strong_affinity_blocks)

# Select top blocks for detailed analysis
top_affinity_blocks <- head(strong_affinity_blocks$block, 12)  # Top 12 blocks

# ===== CHART 1: OVERALL BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY HEATMAP =====

# Prepare data for heatmap (top varieties in top blocks)
top_varieties_in_blocks <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks) %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(total_across_blocks = sum(total_surface_ha), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_across_blocks)) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  pull(variety)

heatmap_data <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks, variety %in% top_varieties_in_blocks) %>%
  select(block, variety, variety_percentage) %>%
  complete(block, variety, fill = list(variety_percentage = 0))

# PLOT 1: Heatmap of variety affinity by block
p1 <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = variety, y = block, fill = variety_percentage)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Surface\n(%)", option = "plasma", 
                       trans = "sqrt", labels = function(x) paste0(round(x), "%")) +
  labs(
    title = "Block-Variety Affinity Matrix",
    subtitle = "Percentage of block surface area by variety (stronger affinities in brighter colors)",
    x = "Variety",
    y = "Block"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p1)

# ===== CHART 2: EVOLUTION OF AFFINITY OVER TIME =====

# Enhanced function to find varieties that make up specified percentage of area
find_dominant_varieties_by_threshold <- function(data, threshold = 80) {
  # Data is already filtered for specific block-campaign, just find dominant varieties
  block_campaign_data <- data %>%
    arrange(desc(surface_ha)) %>%
    mutate(
      cumulative_percentage = cumsum(surface_ha) / sum(surface_ha) * 100,
      is_dominant = cumulative_percentage <= threshold
    )
  
  # Get varieties that together make up the threshold percentage
  dominant_varieties <- block_campaign_data %>%
    filter(is_dominant) %>%
    pull(variety)
  
  return(dominant_varieties)
}

# Calculate variety percentage by block and campaign with dynamic selection
affinity_evolution_raw <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks[1:8]) %>%  # Top 8 blocks for readability
  group_by(block, campaign, variety) %>%
  summarise(surface_ha = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(block, campaign) %>%
  mutate(
    campaign_total = sum(surface_ha),
    variety_percentage = (surface_ha / campaign_total) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# For each block-campaign combination, find varieties that make up ~80% of area
affinity_evolution <- affinity_evolution_raw %>%
  group_by(block, campaign) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    # Find dominant varieties (those that together make up 80% of area)
    dominant_vars <- find_dominant_varieties_by_threshold(.x, threshold = 80)
    
    # Return only dominant varieties
    .x %>% filter(variety %in% dominant_vars)
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Get all unique varieties that appear as dominant across all block-campaign combinations
all_dominant_varieties <- unique(affinity_evolution$variety)

# Create more distinct color palette using multiple color schemes
create_distinct_colors <- function(n) {
  if (n <= 8) {
    # Use Set1 for small numbers (most distinct)
    colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(min(n, 8), "Set1")
  } else if (n <= 12) {
    # Combine Set1 and Dark2
    colors <- c(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set1"), 
                RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(min(n-8, 4), "Dark2"))
  } else {
    # For many varieties, use viridis with distinct endpoints
    colors <- viridis::viridis(n, option = "turbo", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9)
  }
  return(colors[1:n])
}

colors_affinity <- create_distinct_colors(length(all_dominant_varieties))
names(colors_affinity) <- all_dominant_varieties

cat("Using", length(all_dominant_varieties), "varieties that represent ~80% of area in each block-campaign\n")
cat("Dominant varieties found:", paste(all_dominant_varieties, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# PLOT 2: Evolution of variety dominance over time by block (enhanced)
p2 <- ggplot(affinity_evolution, aes(x = campaign, y = variety_percentage, fill = variety)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.7, color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_affinity, name = "Variety") +
  facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Evolution of Variety Dominance by Block Over Time",
    subtitle = "Varieties representing ~80% of block surface area per campaign (more distinct colors)",
    x = "Campaign",
    y = "Surface Area Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 0.8)))

print(p2)

# ===== CHART 3: DOMINANT VARIETY STABILITY INDEX =====

# Calculate stability of dominant varieties over time
variety_stability <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks) %>%
  group_by(block, campaign) %>%
  summarise(
    dominant_variety = variety[which.max(surface_area_ha)],
    dominant_percentage = max(surface_area_ha) / sum(surface_area_ha) * 100,
    total_varieties = n_distinct(variety),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(block) %>%
  summarise(
    campaigns_count = n(),
    unique_dominants = n_distinct(dominant_variety),
    most_frequent_dominant = names(sort(table(dominant_variety), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    dominant_frequency = max(table(dominant_variety)) / campaigns_count,
    avg_dominant_percentage = mean(dominant_percentage),
    stability_score = dominant_frequency * avg_dominant_percentage / 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(stability_score))

# PLOT 3: Block variety stability index
p3 <- ggplot(variety_stability, aes(x = reorder(block, stability_score), y = stability_score)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = most_frequent_dominant), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = most_frequent_dominant), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Most Frequent\nDominant Variety", option = "plasma") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Block Variety Stability Index",
    subtitle = "Stability = (Dominance Frequency) × (Average Dominance Percentage)",
    x = "Block",
    y = "Stability Score"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p3)

# ===== CHART 4: VARIETY SPECIALIZATION BY BLOCK =====

# Calculate specialization index (how much more a variety is present in a block vs overall)
overall_variety_distribution <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(overall_percentage = sum(surface_area_ha) / sum(analysis_data$surface_area_ha) * 100, 
            .groups = "drop")

specialization_data <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks, variety_percentage > 5) %>%  # Only significant presences
  left_join(overall_variety_distribution, by = "variety") %>%
  mutate(
    specialization_index = variety_percentage / overall_percentage,
    is_specialized = specialization_index > 1.5  # 50% more than average
  ) %>%
  filter(specialization_index > 1.2) %>%  # Only show varieties with some specialization
  arrange(desc(specialization_index))

# PLOT 4: Variety specialization by block
p4 <- ggplot(specialization_data, aes(x = reorder(paste(block, variety, sep = " - "), specialization_index), 
                                      y = specialization_index)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = variety), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Variety", option = "turbo") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Block-Variety Specialization Index",
    subtitle = "Values > 1 indicate higher than average presence (red line = average)",
    x = "Block - Variety",
    y = "Specialization Index (Block % / Overall %)"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p4)

# ===== SUMMARY STATISTICS AND INSIGHTS =====

cat("\n=== BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY INSIGHTS ===\n")

cat("STRONGEST VARIETY AFFINITIES:\n")
strongest_affinities <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  filter(variety_percentage > 30) %>%
  arrange(desc(variety_percentage)) %>%
  select(block, variety, variety_percentage, total_surface_ha, campaigns_present)

print(head(strongest_affinities, 10))

cat("\nBLOCK DIVERSITY ANALYSIS:\n")
block_diversity <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  group_by(block) %>%
  summarise(
    total_varieties = n(),
    shannon_diversity = -sum((variety_percentage/100) * log(variety_percentage/100)),
    simpson_diversity = 1 - sum((variety_percentage/100)^2),
    evenness = shannon_diversity / log(total_varieties),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(shannon_diversity))

print(head(block_diversity, 10))

cat("\nMOST SPECIALIZED BLOCK-VARIETY COMBINATIONS:\n")
print(head(specialization_data %>% 
            select(block, variety, variety_percentage, specialization_index), 10))

cat("\nVARIETY LOYALTY BY BLOCK (blocks that consistently grow the same dominant variety):\n")
loyalty_summary <- variety_stability %>%
  filter(dominant_frequency > 0.7) %>%  # Blocks where same variety dominates >70% of time
  select(block, most_frequent_dominant, dominant_frequency, avg_dominant_percentage, stability_score) %>%
  arrange(desc(stability_score))

print(loyalty_summary)

# Calculate some key insights
total_blocks_analyzed <- n_distinct(block_variety_affinity$block)
blocks_with_strong_preference <- nrow(strong_affinity_blocks)
most_versatile_variety <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(blocks_present = n_distinct(block), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(blocks_present)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1)
```

```{r}
# Block-Variety Affinity Analysis Extension (50% Threshold)
# Analyzing variety preferences and dominance patterns by block over time
if (!require(ggplot2)) library(ggplot2)
if (!require(dplyr)) library(dplyr)
if (!require(tidyr)) library(tidyr)
if (!require(RColorBrewer)) library(RColorBrewer)
if (!require(viridis)) library(viridis)
if (!require(scales)) library(scales)
if (!require(gridExtra)) library(gridExtra)

cat("=== BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY ANALYSIS (50% THRESHOLD) ===\n")

# Ensure we have the necessary data (from previous analysis)
if (!exists("analysis_data")) {
  stop("Error: 'analysis_data' not found. Please run the main variety analysis script first.")
}

# Convert variety names to uppercase for consistency
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(variety = toupper(variety))

cat("Variety names converted to uppercase\n")

# Use the same theme from previous analysis
if (!exists("theme_custom")) {
  theme_custom <- function() {
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 8)),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray80")
    )
  }
}

# ===== BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY CALCULATIONS =====

# Calculate variety dominance by block across all campaigns
block_variety_affinity <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(block, variety) %>%
  summarise(
    total_surface_ha = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_parcels = n(),
    campaigns_present = n_distinct(campaign),
    avg_parcel_size = mean(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Calculate percentage within each block
  group_by(block) %>%
  mutate(
    block_total_surface = sum(total_surface_ha),
    variety_percentage = (total_surface_ha / block_total_surface) * 100,
    variety_rank = rank(desc(total_surface_ha), ties.method = "first")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Filter for meaningful blocks (at least 10 ha total)
  filter(block_total_surface >= 10)

# Identify blocks with strong variety preferences (where top variety > 25% or top 3 varieties > 70%)
strong_affinity_blocks <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  group_by(block) %>%
  summarise(
    top1_percentage = max(variety_percentage),
    top3_percentage = sum(head(sort(variety_percentage, decreasing = TRUE), 3)),
    dominant_variety = variety[which.max(variety_percentage)],
    total_varieties = n_distinct(variety),
    total_surface = first(block_total_surface),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(top1_percentage > 25 | top3_percentage > 70) %>%  # Blocks with clear preferences
  arrange(desc(top1_percentage))

# Select top blocks for detailed analysis
top_affinity_blocks <- head(strong_affinity_blocks$block, 12)  # Top 12 blocks

# ===== CHART 1: OVERALL BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY HEATMAP =====

# Prepare data for heatmap (top varieties in top blocks)
top_varieties_in_blocks <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks) %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%
  summarise(total_across_blocks = sum(total_surface_ha), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_across_blocks)) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  pull(variety)

heatmap_data <- block_variety_affinity %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks, variety %in% top_varieties_in_blocks) %>%
  select(block, variety, variety_percentage) %>%
  complete(block, variety, fill = list(variety_percentage = 0))

# PLOT 1: Heatmap of variety affinity by block
p1_50 <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = variety, y = block, fill = variety_percentage)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Surface\n(%)", option = "plasma", 
                       trans = "sqrt", labels = function(x) paste0(round(x), "%")) +
  labs(
    title = "Block-Variety Affinity Matrix (50% Analysis)",
    subtitle = "Percentage of block surface area by variety (stronger affinities in brighter colors)",
    x = "Variety",
    y = "Block"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p1_50)

# ===== CHART 2: EVOLUTION OF AFFINITY OVER TIME (50% THRESHOLD) =====

# Enhanced function to find varieties that make up specified percentage of area
find_dominant_varieties_by_threshold_50 <- function(data, threshold = 50) {
  # Data is already filtered for specific block-campaign, just find dominant varieties
  block_campaign_data <- data %>%
    arrange(desc(surface_ha)) %>%
    mutate(
      cumulative_percentage = cumsum(surface_ha) / sum(surface_ha) * 100,
      is_dominant = cumulative_percentage <= threshold
    )
  
  # Get varieties that together make up the threshold percentage
  dominant_varieties <- block_campaign_data %>%
    filter(is_dominant) %>%
    pull(variety)
  
  return(dominant_varieties)
}

# Calculate variety percentage by block and campaign with dynamic selection
affinity_evolution_raw_50 <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks[1:8]) %>%  # Top 8 blocks for readability
  group_by(block, campaign, variety) %>%
  summarise(surface_ha = sum(surface_area_ha, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(block, campaign) %>%
  mutate(
    campaign_total = sum(surface_ha),
    variety_percentage = (surface_ha / campaign_total) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# For each block-campaign combination, find varieties that make up ~50% of area
affinity_evolution_50 <- affinity_evolution_raw_50 %>%
  group_by(block, campaign) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    # Find dominant varieties (those that together make up 50% of area)
    dominant_vars <- find_dominant_varieties_by_threshold_50(.x, threshold = 50)
    
    # Return only dominant varieties
    .x %>% filter(variety %in% dominant_vars)
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Get all unique varieties that appear as dominant across all block-campaign combinations
all_dominant_varieties_50 <- unique(affinity_evolution_50$variety)

# Create more distinct color palette using multiple color schemes
create_distinct_colors <- function(n) {
  if (n <= 8) {
    # Use Set1 for small numbers (most distinct)
    colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(min(n, 8), "Set1")
  } else if (n <= 12) {
    # Combine Set1 and Dark2
    colors <- c(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set1"), 
                RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(min(n-8, 4), "Dark2"))
  } else {
    # For many varieties, use viridis with distinct endpoints
    colors <- viridis::viridis(n, option = "turbo", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9)
  }
  return(colors[1:n])
}

colors_affinity_50 <- create_distinct_colors(length(all_dominant_varieties_50))
names(colors_affinity_50) <- all_dominant_varieties_50

cat("Using", length(all_dominant_varieties_50), "varieties that represent ~50% of area in each block-campaign\n")
cat("Dominant varieties found:", paste(all_dominant_varieties_50, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# PLOT 2: Evolution of variety dominance over time by block (50% threshold)
p2_50 <- ggplot(affinity_evolution_50, aes(x = campaign, y = variety_percentage, fill = variety)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.7, color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_affinity_50, name = "Variety") +
  facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Evolution of Variety Dominance by Block Over Time (50% Threshold)",
    subtitle = "Varieties representing ~50% of block surface area per campaign (more distinct colors)",
    x = "Campaign",
    y = "Surface Area Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 0.8)))

print(p2_50)

# ===== CHART 3: DOMINANT VARIETY STABILITY INDEX =====

# Calculate stability of dominant varieties over time
variety_stability_50 <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(block %in% top_affinity_blocks) %>%
  group_by(block, campaign) %>%
  summarise(
    dominant_variety = variety[which.max(surface_area_ha)],
    dominant_percentage = max(surface_area_ha) / sum(surface_area_ha) * 100,
    total_varieties = n_distinct(variety),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(block) %>%
  summarise(
    campaigns_count = n(),
    unique_dominants = n_distinct(dominant_variety),
    most_frequent_dominant = names(sort(table(dominant_variety), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    dominant_frequency = max(table(dominant_variety)) / campaigns_count,
    avg_dominant_percentage = mean(dominant_percentage),
    stability_score = dominant_frequency * avg_dominant_percentage / 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(stability_score))

# PLOT 3: Block variety stability index (50% analysis)
p3_50 <- ggplot(variety_stability_50, aes(x = reorder(block, stability_score), y = stability_score)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = most_frequent_dominant), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = most_frequent_dominant), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Most Frequent\nDominant Variety", option = "plasma") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Block Variety Stability Index (50% Analysis)",
    subtitle = "Stability = (Dominance Frequency) × (Average Dominance Percentage)",
    x = "Block",
    y = "Stability Score"
  ) +
  theme_custom() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p3_50)

# ===== CHART 4: VARIETY SPECIALIZATION BY BLOCK =====

# Calculate specialization index (how much more a variety is present in a block vs overall)
overall_variety_distribution_50 <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(variety) %>%

specialization_data_50 <- block_variety_affinity %>%

# PLOT 4: Variety specialization by block (50% analysis)
p4_50 <- ggplot(specialization_data_50, aes(x = reorder(paste(block, variety, sep = " - "), specialization_index), 
                                            y = specialization_index)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = variety), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Variety", option = "turbo") +

  ) +
  theme_custom() +

print(p4_50)

# ===== SUMMARY STATISTICS AND INSIGHTS =====

cat("\n=== BLOCK-VARIETY AFFINITY INSIGHTS (50% THRESHOLD) ===\n")

cat("STRONGEST VARIETY AFFINITIES:\n")
strongest_affinities_50 <- block_variety_affinity %>%

print(head(strongest_affinities_50, 10))

    simpson_diversity = 1 - sum((variety_percentage/100)^2),

print(head(block_diversity_50, 10))
```
